acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ Written BEFORE the code, unlike ACC-0001..0009. `not-evaluated` is the honest state and is exactly the distinction QST-0015 was about: the criterion exists, the work does not. ⚠️ EVALUATED 2026-08-22: `test/handoff.test.mjs` covers it in four parts — a slice carries its tasks' requirements, criteria and components; a cross-role dependency is visible to the blocked role; no tasks means no slices; and slugs are stable. ⚠️ The cross-role case is covered by a CONSTRUCTED fixture, because this project has exactly one role — so the case the criterion is really about has been tested but not lived.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each role in the task graph, the generated slice contains every task assigned to that role together with the requirements and acceptance criteria those tasks trace to, and nothing is a reference to a file outside the package.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every role slice is self-sufficient

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Evaluated 2026-08-22 by test/stage-scope.test.mjs. `stage6Scope` computes the set from `restsOn` on ACTIVE instruction-bearing artifacts, and a name check asserts the module never mentions `loadBearing` (comments stripped first, per the #142 lesson). ⚠️ Falsified: replacing the derivation with a `loadBearing` filter fails four tests, including this criterion's own.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The set of assertions stage 6 checks is computed from `restsOn` on active runbook steps (and any other graph use decided at the time), and contains no reference to the `loadBearing` field.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stage 6's scope is derived from the graph, not from a flag

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Evaluated 2026-08-22 by test/stage-scope.test.mjs. An assertion whose `loadBearing` is absent OR false is in scope when an active step rests on it — the exact case that passed vacuously (RBS-0001 on AST-0002). ⚠️ CONSTRUCTED, and it had to be: RBS-0001 was retired, so the live graph no longer contains the case its own finding was about.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given a runbook step resting on an assertion whose `loadBearing` is absent or false, that assertion appears in stage 6's evaluated set. This is the exact case that passes vacuously today: RBS-0001 rests on AST-0002, which is unflagged.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An unflagged premise of an active runbook step is in scope

acceptanceCriteria.notes: This is the clause that stops a page-level boundary satisfying DEC-0019 on paper. One boundary wrapping everything makes the whole page the fallback, which technically has a loading state and buys nothing.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The initial HTML of the stage view contains a distinct loading fallback for the exit-criteria region and for the stage-document region. Delaying either read leaves the other region's content rendered and only its own fallback showing.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The stage view's reads resolve behind separate boundaries

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE LAST SENTENCE IS THE WHOLE CRITERION. Stripping also produces a page with no executed code, so a test that renders a document and looks for a side effect passes identically on rejection and on silent removal — which is exactly the distinction the amendment to DEC-0020 exists to preserve. The observable being checked is the refusal, not the absence.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each of an ESM import, an ESM export, a flow expression, a text expression, a JSX attribute expression, a JSX spread attribute, and a JSX element outside the permitted set: compiling a stage document containing it produces a FAILURE that names the document path and a line:column position. A document that merely renders without the forbidden construct's effect is a FAIL for this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Each forbidden construct FAILS the compile with a file and position

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The negative criteria above are satisfiable by a compiler that refuses everything. This is the control that stops that.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A stage document containing markdown and only components from the permitted set compiles, renders its markdown structure, and renders each permitted component it uses.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A permitted document renders, including its mapped components

acceptanceCriteria.notes: AST-0030 measured file-routed `@next/mdx` failing exactly this: the document is compiled into the build and an edit changes nothing. That configuration satisfies REQ-0017 and silently fails REQ-0018, which is why this is a criterion rather than an implementation note.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With the built application serving, editing a stage document on disk changes what the next request for that stage returns, with no rebuild and no restart.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stage documents compile at request time, not at build time

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ 'Without executing the application' is load-bearing. AST-0022 measured that a non-compliant read is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route, so every behavioural check passes on a codebase that violates the contract until the compliant sibling moves.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A check that runs WITHOUT executing the application reports a failure naming file and line when any module other than the planning-content reader performs a filesystem read rooted at the content directory.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check fails on a planning-content read outside the reader

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The clause that gets dropped. An abstraction can supply `connection()` while a caller omits the boundary; that builds fine without Cache Components and fails the build with it, so the omission would surface as an unrelated configuration change breaking the build.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The same non-executing check reports a failure when a planning-content read site is not enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary, naming file and line.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check fails on a read outside a Suspense boundary

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The indirect clause is the bypass path DEC-0021 requires be detected. A direct import is easy to find; a module that re-exports `lib/` and is then imported freely is the same violation wearing one layer.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The same non-executing check reports a failure naming file and line when any module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, including through a re-export chain that reaches `lib/` indirectly.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check fails on an app module importing `lib/` directly

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ ADDED BECAUSE IT HAPPENED. A refusal test written during this work passed with the refusal deleted — the assertion that mattered sat behind a condition that was never true. A check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. This criterion is what makes the three above mean something rather than merely exist.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The check is evaluated against a fixture set containing at least one instance of each violation it claims to detect, and reports a failure for every one. A check that passes the fixture set is a FAIL for this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The boundary check is itself falsified against known violations

acceptanceCriteria.notes: `export *` would make the adapter a hole rather than a door: the exposed surface would widen every time `lib/` gains an export, including locking and process-spawning modules, with no diff for anyone to review.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every module under `app/server/` has `import 'server-only'` as its first statement and contains no `export *`. Checked statically over the whole directory, with no exemptions.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every adapter module is guarded and explicitly exported

acceptanceCriteria.notes: AST-0033 measured `server-only` throwing outside the RSC compiler. This criterion is what stops the guard migrating into `lib/` later as a tidy-up and breaking the tool to protect the app.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every command under `bin/` and the full test suite run to completion with the shell present, importing `lib/` directly under plain Node with no RSC compiler in play.
acceptanceCriteria.title: `lib/` stays importable under plain Node

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE WORDING CLAUSE IS MEASURED, NOT STYLISTIC. Next.js produced two different messages for the same violation reached two ways, and one of them said 'you are using it in the Pages Router' for an App Router project. A test pinned to that string would pass on a wrong message today and break on a corrected one after an upgrade.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A `'use client'` module importing any `app/server/` adapter causes the build to fail with a message naming the offending file and a line:column position. The criterion asserts the presence of a file and a position, and MUST NOT assert the diagnostic's wording.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A client component reaching an adapter fails the build, locatably

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ AST-0036: a line beginning with a colon is ignored by the client parser, so a comment heartbeat keeps the socket warm and fires nothing. The criterion is the listener firing, not bytes arriving, because bytes arriving was never the problem.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: While connected and with no content changing, the stream delivers an event with a name and a data field at least once per configured heartbeat interval, and a client listener registered for that event name fires. A comment-only keepalive is a FAIL for this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The stream emits a named heartbeat event that page code can observe

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The operator is looking at a browser, not a terminal. A logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect in its purest form: the system knows, records it accurately, and tells the person who needs it nothing.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: When the file watcher fails, the page shows the stale indication or the stream closes. A run in which the failure appears only in server output while the page continues to indicate health is a FAIL.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A watcher failure reaches the page, never only a log

acceptanceCriteria.notes: 'Verified by observation, not by the absence of an error' is the tier-1 controller's own rule arriving here: a removal that reports success while the directory survives is retained, and the check has to be `exists()` rather than `!threw`. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-29: THERE IS NO SECOND PROCESS, AND THERE NEVER WAS ONE TO OWN. This artifact previously said the launcher owns 'both the application process and the file watcher' and 'terminates the watcher with the application'. The watcher is chokidar, imported dynamically INSIDE the `next start` process and held by the change-stream service in that process's memory. A parent launcher cannot call `changeStream.close()` across that boundary without adding IPC or a shutdown endpoint, and neither is justified for a local-first tool. The old wording described a mechanism that could not be built, which is worse than an unmet obligation: it would have been 'satisfied' by a launcher that called nothing and reported success. ⚠️ WHAT IS TRUE INSTEAD, and all of it is enforceable. The launcher owns ONE child: the `next start` process. The change-stream service owns its watcher and closes it when its last subscriber leaves — already built and tested under TSK-0011. Terminating the application process releases any watcher still open through process teardown, which is the operating system's guarantee rather than the launcher's. `close()` stays what it is: a service and test lifecycle operation, never something the launcher claims to call across a process boundary. ⚠️ THIS CRITERION WAS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AMENDED RATHER THAN REPHRASED. It required that 'no watcher process remains'. There is no watcher process, so the clause could never be observed either true or false — and an unobservable clause in a criterion whose whole point is 'verified by observation, not by the absence of an error' is the exact defect that rule exists to catch, sitting inside the rule. It is amended rather than superseded because it has never been evaluated: no measurement is being retired, and there is no failed outcome to preserve. ⚠️ THE HEARTBEAT PRECONDITION IS PART OF THE CRITERION, not of the test that runs it. The watcher is created lazily on first subscription, so a run that never subscribed would satisfy every remaining clause while having nothing to clean up.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: After the documented launch command is run and then terminated, the child process it started is gone, no process is listening on the application's port, and no temporary directory the launcher created survives — each verified by observation, not by the absence of an error. The run must have opened `/events` and observed a heartbeat before termination, so that a file watcher is known to have existed.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stopping the launcher leaves nothing behind

acceptanceCriteria.notes: 'No further steps' is the testable half. DEC-0018 fixes the mode: `next build` then `next start`, never the development server. ⚠️ MARKED `pass` IN ERROR ON 2026-08-29 AND RETURNED TO `not-evaluated` THE SAME DAY. EVD-0073 recorded, in its own omissions, that the install branch was never taken: `node_modules` was present in every run, so the launcher printed `dependencies present; skipping install`. This criterion says 'on a machine with... no prior application state' and 'installs and starts'. Half of it was measured and the whole of it was ticked. ⚠️ THE EVIDENCE ITSELF SAID SO, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. The omission was written down accurately and then contradicted by the outcome three lines later — a criterion marked against evidence that explicitly disclaims the thing being claimed. Recording an omission is not the same as honouring it. ⚠️ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the documented command run in a disposable copy of the repository with no `node_modules` and no `.next`, installing, building, serving and cleaning up with no further steps. ⚠️ EVALUATED PROPERLY 2026-08-29 (EVD-0074) AND RETURNED TO `pass`. The documented command was run in a disposable copy holding only tracked files, with `node_modules` and `.next` confirmed absent. It installed, built, served and cleaned up in 27.2s with no further steps, and the install branch was asserted positively rather than inferred from the run succeeding.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: On a machine with the repository and Node present and no prior application state, the documented command installs and starts the application in production mode, and the project view responds, without further steps. The install is conditional and the command says which branch it took: a cold checkout installs; a warm checkout whose root lockfile is not newer than npm's installed-tree marker skips the install; and a missing or stale marker installs rather than guessing about a tree npm did not lay down. ⚠️ THE FRESHNESS COMPARISON IS AGAINST npm's MARKER, NOT THE `node_modules` DIRECTORY mtime. A directory's mtime moves only when an entry is added or removed at its top level, which reinstalling the same tree does not do, while `npm install` touches the lockfile every time — so comparing the two made the condition permanently true and the documented command reinstalled on every start, which is the outcome a conditional install exists to prevent.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The application installs and starts from one documented command

acceptanceCriteria.notes: The byte-identical clause is what makes this objective rather than a claim about intent. #82's two-axis split is the reason `lifecycle` is named explicitly: one `status` field would have let this endpoint retire an artifact by accident.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The review action identifies the artifact by id and type and shows its current status. Submitting a change updates only that artifact's `reviewStatus`, through the existing typed write path with its lock and atomic write; the artifact's `lifecycle` and every other artifact on disk are byte-identical afterwards.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A review update changes one artifact's reviewStatus and nothing else

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ IT SUCCEEDS ACC-0020 AND IT IS NOT ACC-0020 WITH A BIGGER NUMBER. The predecessor bounded read-plus-compile at 300 ms and failed, but the measurement showed the failure came from the read. Widening that budget would have hidden a real unknown behind a comfortable ceiling. This one bounds only the cost that was ever in dispute — whether request-time MDX compilation is affordable — and the read it excluded is carried by its own open question, not dropped. ⚠️ 50 ms IS ROUGHLY TWICE THE MEASURED WORST CASE (29.05 ms p95 across six runs), chosen as headroom for document growth rather than as a description of today. A criterion set at the measurement passes by construction and detects nothing. ⚠️ THE VERIFICATION CLAUSE IS INHERITED DELIBERATELY, and it has been falsified: memoising the compiled document makes `bin/bench-compile.mjs` report VOID with a non-zero exit and no timing figures at all. Without it the cheapest way to pass a compile budget is to stop compiling, which would also break DEC-0020's request-time requirement and AST-0030's finding beneath it. ⚠️ EVALUATED `pass` ON EVD-0071, the same six runs that failed the predecessor: compile p95 was 15.41-29.05 ms in every one. The evidence did not change; the question it was asked did.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The 95th-percentile time spent in `compileStageDocument` for the largest stage document is at or below 50 ms. MEASURED SPAN: the compile call alone — from the moment the reader's document is handed to the compiler to the moment a renderable component is returned — EXCLUDING the planning-content read that precedes it, which is a separate cost under a separate question. ENVIRONMENT: the reference host, with its OS, Node version, Next.js version, @mdx-js/mdx version and CPU model recorded alongside the result; no other significant load. DOCUMENT: the largest stage document by byte count at the time of evaluation, named in the result. WARM-UP: 10 requests issued and discarded. SAMPLE: the next 50 consecutive requests, issued one at a time with no concurrency. VERIFICATION: the compile counter must advance by exactly one per measured request. A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID, not a pass.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Restricted-MDX compilation stays within 50 ms at p95, under ACC-0020's protocol

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-03. Mechanised in test/pi-compat.test.mjs inside `assertContract()`, which is applied to the retained record AND to the live run: trust rows 4 and 5 revert the grant, the sentinel control shows secrets crossing under inheritance, the prose and exclusion controls show no tool executing, the override-removal control restores the packaged skill, the no-credential control leaves the model unavailable, the without-variable control leaves the env-authenticated model unavailable while an inline-key provider is listed in both, and the default-directory control shows the override actually moved something. ⚠️ TWO GAPS WERE FOUND IN THIS CRITERION'S OWN ENFORCEMENT AND BOTH ARE CLOSED. The packaged prompt proof had only a successful expansion: `literalSlashStringReachedProvider: false` in the SAME run is the other half of one observation, not a control, and would read identically if the template had expanded for a reason unrelated to package loading. There is now a separate run with trust revoked in which the package does not load, the body marker does not arrive, and the literal slash string survives. ⚠️ AND `reachedObservationPoint()` ACCEPTED ANY TERMINATED PROCESS THAT EMITTED ANY OUTPUT — so a CLI dying on a bad argument would have had its missing marker read as a trust result. It now requires a `session` event in the transcript, which is emitted after the point where the load-time marker would have been written. An absent marker beside a session event is a real negative; an absent marker beside no session event is a void run, and the test refuses it.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each behaviour the compatibility suite establishes, the recorded evidence contains both the observation and a control run in which the claimed behaviour is absent and the observation does not appear. A claim recorded with only a positive run fails this criterion, and so does a negative result whose transcript does not show the process reaching the point where the observation would have been made.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every spike claim carries a negative control that would have failed

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-03. Retained results exist for both platforms and each names its platform, Node version and the pinned Pi version. ⚠️ THE TEST ALSO FAILS ON A PIN BUMP: it compares the pin in package.json against the pin the evidence was taken under and refuses a mismatch, naming the command to re-run. That is what stops a version change inheriting the previous version's evidence. POSIX was measured on Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 and the live tier re-runs on ubuntu-latest in CI. ⚠️ 'RECORDS WHICH PLATFORM' NOW MEANS SOMETHING TO THE DERIVATION ENGINE, which it did not before: the environment facts were written as prose — `platform: 'windows and linux'`, `piVersion: '0.84.4, installed by...'` — and the engine compares facts by exact equality, so every supporting record was excluded and ten of twelve spike assertions derived as unverified while reading as proved. Facts are scalars now, prose lives in summaries, and the one observation whose RESULT differs by platform has a single-platform record of its own.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each recorded observation names the platform, the exact pinned Pi version, and the Node version it was taken on, and the suite has been executed to completion on both Windows and the project's supported POSIX CI platform. A behaviour observed on one platform only is recorded as single-platform rather than as the contract.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The suite runs on Windows and on the supported POSIX platform and records which

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-03, AND IT FAILED THREE TIMES FIRST — the sequence is the point. (1) The initial result set was saved unredacted and was full of absolute home paths. (2) The second version redacted the summary while npm's output went straight to the terminal and was captured nowhere, so the test scanned a summary while the criterion said 'command output'. (3) The third still omitted `pi install -l`, the fake provider's streams, and every generated file, and the DETECTOR could not see a Windows home path once JSON-escaped — `C:\\Users\\alice` in serialised bytes returned an empty violation list while the raw string was flagged. ⚠️ NARROWED TO WHAT IS ACTUALLY COVERED, AND THE COVERAGE WIDENED TO MEET IT. The scope is now RETAINED bytes, enumerated; streamed-and-discarded output is explicitly out, because a criterion nothing can check is worse than a narrower one. ⚠️ THE DETECTOR AND THE REDACTOR ARE TESTED AGAINST EACH OTHER, in both directions: every forbidden shape must be SEEN by the detector before the redactor is asked to remove it, and both must handle the JSON-escaped form. They disagreed twice — once with the redactor weaker, once with the detector weaker — and the second is the dangerous direction.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every byte the suite RETAINS is asserted to contain no API key, OAuth token, authorisation header, credential-derived fingerprint, username, or absolute user-home path. What is retained is enumerated and complete: the result summary; the captured stdout and stderr of every subprocess the suite starts, including the consumer's `npm install`, `pi install -l`, every Pi child, the model-registry probes and the fake provider; and the generated state the suite produced — the provider request log, the project settings file and the trust store. The assertion runs over those captured bytes rather than over a summary of them; redaction happens at write time and the runner refuses to save a file that still violates the rule. Output that is streamed and discarded is out of scope, because nothing can scan it.
acceptanceCriteria.title: No spike artefact contains credential material

acceptanceCriteria.statement: With a different Pi version installed globally and earlier on PATH, every Pi process Kiln starts reports the pinned version. A test that removes the local dependency causes a refusal naming the expected version and the resolved path, rather than falling through to the global binary.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Pi is resolved from the tool's node_modules and never from PATH

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-03, mechanised in `test/content-root.test.mjs`. ⚠️ THE TESTS ARE WRITTEN AROUND THE DIVERGENCE, NOT THE AGREEMENT. `dirname(contentRoot)` and `<toolRoot>/..` name the same directory in an ordinary consumer install, so a resolver that took the wrong one would pass every test that did not set the override. The override case therefore asserts BOTH that the answer is the owner of the overridden directory AND that it is not the tool's parent — which is a real directory and a plausible wrong answer. ⚠️ CANONICAL COMPARISON IS PART OF THE CRITERION because without it the refusal misfires: a correct setup invocation arriving by a symlinked path would read as a disagreement, and a refusal that fires on correct input is worse than none. Covered with a junction, skipped rather than failed where symlink creation is privileged. ⚠️ SCOPE: THIS IS THE RESOLVER, AND ONLY THE RESOLVER. The obligation that SETUP calls it — printing every canonicalised path before the first lasting write, and refusing on disagreement — is ACC-0085 against CMP-0039, and is correctly still not-evaluated because setup does not exist. The third clause here previously read as though it were about setup; it is about the thing that does the refusing, which is what can be evaluated now.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR unset, the resolved project root is the parent of the content root derived from the tool location; with it set, it is the canonical parent of that explicit directory and NOT the tool's parent, asserted as a distinct value rather than merely as the right one. Given an explicit project root that disagrees with the resolved content owner, the resolver refuses and its message names both paths, the rule that produced the resolved one, and the override — rather than choosing between them. Comparison is canonical, so two spellings of one directory do not read as a disagreement.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The project root is derived from the resolved content root, and a mismatch refuses

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138. A second run naming nothing reads back the committed selection and this host's approval of it, asks no question, and leaves every file byte-identical — the whole tree by digest rather than a reported status — including the settings file, the ignore block, the identity file and the generated content; the compatibility record too, and the live check is not run again. A third run leaves the identity file's mtime untouched, so nothing is rewritten with identical bytes.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Running setup twice with the same inputs against the same project leaves every file it owns byte-identical, including the settings file, the ignore block, the project identity file and the generated skills. The comparison is over file bytes, not over a reported status.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A rerun with unchanged choices changes no bytes

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When a file the transaction recorded is modified after the plan is built and before the merge runs, the transaction detects the changed identity under the lock and refuses, leaving the operator's edit intact. A malformed or unknown-schema-version file likewise refuses rather than being replaced.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A file edited between plan and merge refuses rather than overwriting

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138, measured by killing real children rather than by making one throw. Inside the bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists: the project is byte-identical afterwards, no `.pi` survives, and an ordinary rerun completes. After the journal opens: what the killed run left records the phase in flight as running — true only because that status is written before the work — and carries an exact resume command naming the project. THE ARGUMENTS ARE PARSED OUT OF THAT COMMAND, not typed beside it, so a command naming another project, omitting `--resume`, or missing altogether fails the control; running them completes the remaining phases and leaves no journal. A failure in an agent phase leaves the scaffold and reports partial setup. THE MEASUREMENT FOUND FIVE DEFECTS IN THE LOCK, EACH FOUND BY THE CONTROL OR THE REVIEW OF THE FIX BEFORE IT, ALL NOW FIXED, AND ALL THE SAME MISTAKE: acting on a judgement about a file that can change, or that never proved what it was read for. A killed run's lockfile made every rerun wait out the two-minute stale window; clearing such a lock by read-then-unlink lets two recoveries both acquire; claiming it by rename moves a lock that went live in the meantime, leaving the name free for a waiter, which four racing recoveries caught in CI; reclaiming the gate introduced for that had the same shape again; and judging a gate abandoned by age treated a process stopped between creating its gate and writing its name into it as dead. Removing somebody else's lock is now serialised behind a gate beside it, taken by the recovery path and the waiter's stale break alike, with the judgement made inside it; reclaiming a gate is serialised by a token and happens only when the gate's record names a process on this host that is demonstrably gone; and nothing reclaims the token. Everything else fails closed: the command refuses with exit code 17 and names both files to remove. Setup still refuses another machine's lock, an unreadable one, and a live one.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Killing setup after its journal has begun leaves a journal naming the last completed phase and an exact resume command; running that command completes the remaining phases. Killing it during the dependency bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists, leaves consumer project state unchanged, and rerunning setup repeats the locked install safely. A failure in any agent phase leaves an already-initialised planning scaffold in place and reports partial setup rather than rolling it back.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An interrupted setup resumes from its journal and never deletes valid content

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ "EXACT UNMODIFIED" IS ENFORCED AS BYTES, AND THE CRITERION'S WORDING IS WHAT DECIDED THAT. Migration replaces bytes rather than appending them, so the question it answers is not "does this look like Kiln's block" but "is this, byte for byte, output nobody has touched". A trimmed comparison answers the first and reads as if it answered the second: an indented rule, a trailing space, a tab, a blank line inside the block or mixed line endings all compare equal, and the edit that is the evidence the block was not Kiln's to replace is what gets destroyed. ⚠️ THE MISSING-FINAL-NEWLINE CASE WAS SETTLED THE OTHER WAY ON PURPOSE. A legacy block whose trailing newline something stripped is short one byte Kiln wrote, so it is modified and is reported rather than migrated. The alternative was to amend this criterion to permit one normalisation, which buys an automatic migration in a rare case at the cost of the criterion no longer meaning what it says. The tolerance survives where it belongs — on an explicit rewrite, where the operator asked and the only duty is not to tidy anything unasked. ⚠️ "REQUIRES AN EXPLICIT CHOICE" IS ABOUT OWNERSHIP, NOT COVERAGE. An edited or malformed block can hold every rule Kiln would have written and still be somebody's own work, so the choice is required whether or not its contents happen to protect the paths. Deriving it from coverage produced a report offering two options and requiring neither. ⚠️ WHAT "NEVER SILENTLY REWRITTEN" TURNED OUT TO COVER, after four review rounds, is wider than a single check: consent is to replacing the bytes the operator was SHOWN, so an answer about one block does not authorise replacing a different one that replaced it, and a plan that reported operator-owned content writes nothing at all — not a create, not an append, not a migration — unless that exact file is still there and the answer was `rewrite`. Deleting the block one has just been told about is a plausible answer to being told about it; the run that recreated it for `keep` is the clearest statement of what this criterion forbids.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A fresh project receives exactly one Kiln-marked block containing `.planning/`, `.pi/sessions/` and `.pi/runtime/`. An exact unmodified legacy block containing only `.planning/` is migrated to the extended block with every byte outside the markers preserved, and the migration is recorded and byte-stable on rerun. A block the operator removed or edited is reported and requires an explicit choice; it is never silently rewritten.
acceptanceCriteria.title: One owner writes the ignore block, and a removed block is not restored

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Merging Kiln's owned fields into a `.pi/settings.json` that carries third-party packages, unrelated keys and a custom key order preserves the value of every unrelated key and every unrelated package entry, and preserves the relative order of ordinary string keys. Integer-like property names follow the order Pi's and JavaScript's JSON parsing and serialization give them, not their original textual position. A file that is not valid JSON, whose root is not an object, or whose Kiln-owned fields hold invalid values is refused before anything is written, and the file is left byte-identical; unknown Pi and third-party fields are preserved rather than refused. Applying the same desired state again changes no bytes and does not change the file's modification time.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The settings merge preserves unrelated content, refuses invalid input, and is byte-stable

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The `.pi/settings.json` content produced by the settings merge and the `.pi/kiln.json` content produced by `ensureProjectId` contain no credential value, token, authorisation header or credential-derived fingerprint, and no absolute user path or `~` home reference, asserted over the bytes each produces.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The settings merge and project record write no secret and no absolute user path

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NARROWED TO WHAT TSK-0031 BUILDS. The criterion asked for interactive setup to OFFER the three choices and for non-interactive setup to REFUSE. There is no setup command yet, so nothing could render them and nothing could be non-interactive about them; what this library produces is the refusal and the choices as data. The integration moved to the criterion on TSK-0060 that owns the setup command. ⚠️ THE ASSERTION IS ABSENCE, NOT A MESSAGE. A warning printed before a directory is created is exactly the failure REQ-0027 names, so the check is that the paths are not there.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With the Kiln ignore block absent, edited, partial or negated, deciding project-local state refuses and creates nothing: the state root and every runtime path it would hold do not exist after the refusal, which is what is asserted rather than that a warning was produced. The refusal carries the three choices as data - append the exact ignore block, with the bytes it would add; external state; stop - each marked available or not, and a block that is present but edited marks the append choice unavailable rather than silently composing new bytes over it.
acceptanceCriteria.title: No state root or runtime path is created while coverage is missing

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE RUNTIME-CAPABILITY GATE MOVED. The criterion said the mode is available only if the pinned runtime supports relocation. Nothing in this library gates availability on a capability check: the mode is a parameter, and relocation support is a property of the pinned runtime, recorded in AST-0047 and measured in EVD-0081 and EVD-0083. Offering the mode only once that support is established belongs with the setup command, and is now part of the criterion on TSK-0060. ⚠️ THE NO-PATH CLAIM IS BOUNDED TO THE RECORD THIS TASK WRITES. `.pi/settings.json` is ACC-0048's, and every committed file a complete setup produces is ACC-0106's.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: In external mode the state root is derived from the platform's own convention for per-user state and the stable non-secret project ID: two different IDs on one machine occupy separate roots, an ID that could traverse never becomes a path component, and a root that is not outside the project is refused rather than used. `.pi/kiln.json` holds the ID and the record version and nothing else, and contains no absolute user path, no home directory and not the project's own path.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The external state root derives from the platform convention and the committed project ID

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NARROWED TO WHAT TSK-0032 BUILDS. The criterion asked for interactive setup to display the path and obtain the decision, for `--trust approve`, and for a non-interactive refusal - none of which can exist before the setup command does. Those moved to the criterion on TSK-0060. What is left is the module and the launch gate, which are this task's to deliver and can be tested today. ⚠️ THE STORE IS THE BOUNDARY. DEC-0027 withdrew writing `trust.json` directly; depending on the exported class is the whole of the difference, so 'through the exported store' is part of the assertion rather than an implementation note. ⚠️ MISSING IS NOT DENIED. An absent decision is a project nobody has been asked about; a denial is an operator's answer. Setup may ask about the first and must not re-ask about the second, so a module that reported both as 'not trusted' would make that impossible one layer up.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The trust decision for this project is read, granted, denied and revoked through `ProjectTrustStore` as exported from the pinned package's root, keyed by the canonical project directory, with no write to Pi's trust file shape and no import of an unexported path. A project with no decision and a project that was denied are distinct outcomes, never collapsed into one. An agent launch over a project whose trust is not approved is refused BEFORE the child is spawned, the planning scaffold is left untouched by that refusal, and the refusal names `bin/start-shell.mjs` as the browser-only way to carry on without an agent.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The trust decision is read and recorded through Pi's exported store, and an unapproved project never launches an agent

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-21 on EVD-0125. The consent boundary is observed at Node's own modules: with the recorder started before the module is imported, nothing touched Pi's authentication store, its custom-model file, a credential variable or the network before the answer, after a decline, or for any answer other than true. A decline reports connections as not inspected, unknown rather than absent. Granted runs are the positive control, showing the recorder detects those reads. CI run 35648974488 passed the tests in all four cells. Consent persistence (TSK-0034) and placement in setup (TSK-0060) are not part of this result.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Before the inspection prompt is answered, no read of Pi's authentication store, no load of the custom-model registry and no credential-variable presence check has occurred — observed by instrumenting those access points, not by reading the code. A declined inspection performs none of them, contacts nothing, and leaves setup honestly partial rather than reporting that nothing is configured.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Nothing is read before permission, and a decline reads nothing at all

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-21 on EVD-0125. The granted result holds provider display names, exact model IDs from getAvailable() and present-or-absent for the research credential, and nothing else; getAll() is never called, and a provider whose status alone says configured is not listed. No network attempt was made and no credential value, header or credential field reached the result. LIMIT: this is configured availability under Pi's registry. No provider request was made or shown to succeed. CI run 35648974488 passed the tests in all four cells.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The presented result contains provider display names, exact model identifiers and present-or-absent for the research credential, and is asserted to contain no key, token, header, environment value or credential-derived fingerprint. No external service is contacted during the inspection.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Inspection results report availability and never credential material

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NOT EVALUATED, 2026-09-22. EVD-0126 is component proof for TSK-0034: clone controls for project-local and per-user state, negative controls for a force-added record (R1), a staged but uncommitted removal (R5) and an unignored record in a parent repository (R6), and the no-Git limit (R4). EVD-0127 is component proof for TSK-0035: the research choice writer clears this host's research grant before it writes the choice, so Tavily to none to Tavily asks again, and a failed probe changes nothing. EVD-0128 is component proof for TSK-0036: the model selection writer clears this host's model-use grant before it writes a changed selection, refuses the change when the grant cannot be cleared, and changing away and back reopens approval. This criterion is evaluated once setup (TSK-0060) and the launch path (TSK-0037) exercise these writers and grants.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A project carrying a committed research choice, opened on a machine with no local consent record, reopens the prompt and does not use that host's credential until it is answered. Changing the provider or the research choice likewise reopens the relevant prompt.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A clone does not inherit the first operator's consent

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NOT EVALUATED, 2026-09-22. EVD-0128 is component proof for TSK-0036: a single listed model is shown by display name and exact ID and confirmed before it is assigned, no answer other than a listed number chooses anything, Pi's global default is never read, and a committed selection is not used on a host without confirmation. This criterion is evaluated once setup (TSK-0060) exercises the path.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: When discovery returns exactly one usable model, setup displays its provider display name and exact identifier and requires confirmation before assigning it. Pi's global default and the first entry in discovery order are never adopted implicitly, and a mutable alias is never selected on the operator's behalf.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A single available model still requires confirmation, and no default is adopted

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-22 on EVD-0132, measured through the real start command with its own launch checks. With the recorded model removed from Pi's catalogue, the run refuses naming openai and that exact id and says no other model was used in its place; with the authentication store empty and the credential variable empty, it refuses naming the recorded ids and says no other provider was used in its place. Both refusals carry the two remedies — rerun setup, or start once with --provider <id> --model <id> --thinking <level> — the supervisor is never reached, and the command exits 2. A compatibility record taken under other conditions is refused by the differing determinant before anything starts, and a host without model-use consent is refused with zero reads of any auth.json or models.json, zero credential-variable reads and no network. On the accepted path Pi is held to exactly the checked selection. CI run 35759728422 passed the 12 launch-path tests in all four cells. LIMITS: no billable provider was called, so the one-run override's own live check is proved at the component level (EVD-0130, EVD-0131) rather than through this command against a real provider; a custom provider cannot launch until the command can supply its credential declaration and provider configuration (D25); and the command checks project-local state only (D24).
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With the recorded model removed from the registry, or its authentication absent, launch refuses and names the recorded provider and model, offering a setup rerun or an explicit one-run override. No other model, provider, or answer from model memory is substituted.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An unavailable recorded selection refuses instead of falling back

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE CONTROL IS PART OF THE CRITERION, not a nicety. A sentinel test with no control passes identically whether the boundary works or the sentinels were never set. ⚠️ IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN AS 'the child sees only the union', which was the first phrasing and is not achievable: Windows injects nine home and user variables into every child regardless of the environment supplied (AST-0045). What is provable on both platforms is that no secret Kiln did not choose to pass is among what the child receives.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With unrelated secrets present in the parent environment under names a naive implementation would match, a spawned specialist child's observed environment contains none of them, while a control child spawned with the environment inherited observes all of them. Kiln adds to the child only the measured base variables, the selected provider's declared model-plane names and that role's tool-plane names. The assertion is made over what the child observed, not over what the parent intended.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A sentinel host secret never reaches a child, against a control that shows one crossing

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A provider whose credential contract is neither built in nor declared through the validated custom shape yields an `unsupported-credential-contract` refusal naming the provider. No additional variables are inherited, and no variable name is inferred from the provider id or discovered by scanning the environment.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An unknown environment-only provider is refused, not widened

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The research child receives the research credential when research is enabled and not otherwise; planning and validation children never receive it in any configuration.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Research holds the only tool-plane credential, and only while enabled

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NOT EVALUATED, 2026-09-22. EVD-0131 is component proof for TSK-0042: the section 6.4 prompt names the provider, the exact model and the possible charge; declining is a choice with no request and no record; a run that cannot ask needs --live-model-check approve. Setup does not yet call the check (TSK-0060).
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The prompt names the exact provider and model and states that the provider may charge. Declining leaves a valid content and browser setup, does not mark the agent ready, does not begin intake, and is reported as a choice rather than a failure. Non-interactive runs require an explicit approval flag when no matching record exists.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The canary is separately approved, names the cost, and declining is not an error

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NOT EVALUATED, 2026-09-22. EVD-0130 is component proof for TSK-0041: through Pi's real openai-completions client to a loopback endpoint, only an exact call with this run's challenge passes, and prose, malformed, extra, wrong, repeated and other-tool calls each fail under their own reason. No billable provider was called and the canary does not yet run in setup.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The canary passes only when the model invokes the setup-only tool with the exact random challenge against the declared schema, observed through the real pinned runtime and provider path. A response that merely claims tool support, or that calls the tool with a malformed argument, fails.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Success requires an observed tool call with the right challenge and schema

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-22 (Q6). The statement named the package capability signature as an invalidation input. DEC-0033 and section 3.12 of the proposal replaced it with determinant 8, preflightContractDigest, which digests the canary protocol as handed to Pi: keying on the whole signature charged for a new billable canary whenever an unrelated planning tool changed, while the canary runs with only the preflight tool exposed. The signature is kept as a zero-cost launch check (lib/launch-checks.mjs step 6). Not evaluated: EVD-0130 is component proof for TSK-0041, and the record and its key are TSK-0042's. EVD-0131 adds TSK-0042's component proof: each determinant reopens approval, the key is computed from the request the canary actually made (R8) and its effective endpoint (R9), and a tracked or unprotected record is never reused. Still not evaluated.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: During the canary no planning content is sent and no mutation tool is reachable; the setup-only tool is absent from the user-facing orchestrator and from every specialist. The stored success record contains no credential or credential-derived value, and changing the provider, model, thinking level, runtime version, preflight contract digest or endpoint identity invalidates it and reopens approval. The package capability signature is not part of the record's key; it remains a zero-cost check at every launch.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The canary cannot see or change planning content, and its record invalidates correctly

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NARROWED TO THE PACKAGE ITSELF. The criterion asked for the package's TOOLS to load, which is TSK-0044 and TSK-0045's work on CMP-0032, and those depend on this task - so as written it could not be satisfied until its own dependants were finished. What this asserts is the unit: a manifest whose resources exist, an entry point that loads, a declaration that agrees with the manifest, and Pi finding those resources when the project is trusted and not finding them when it is not. ⚠️ WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: the final Kiln tool set (ACC-0064), the write discipline of each wrapper (ACC-0065), that the registered capability tool returns this declaration (the TSK-0045 criterion below), that a child without the signature is refused (ACC-0075), that the canary's record invalidates on drift (ACC-0062), or that a launch over an untrusted project is refused (ACC-0051, already passing). ⚠️ THE UNTRUSTED CONTROL IS NOT OPTIONAL. `pi-compat` measured what an untrusted run does on 0.84.4: it loads no package and reports nothing. A positive result with no control would read the same way whether the package loaded or Pi simply behaved as it always does.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: `pi-package/package.json` is a valid manifest whose declared extension, skill and prompt resources all exist in the package, and its registration entry point loads without error. A versioned, machine-readable signature declaration is exposed by the package and agrees with that manifest: the resources it names are the resources the manifest declares, neither more nor fewer. A real Pi run over a trusted project discovers those package-owned resources, and the same run over an untrusted project discovers none of them - the control that makes the positive result mean something rather than describing what Pi would have done anyway.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The package declares what it owns, loads under trust, and is absent without it

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The user-facing session's measured active tool set contains the registered Kiln tools and does not contain Pi's built-in shell, write or edit tools. The measurement is of the session's reported registry, not of what the launch options requested.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The orchestrator holds Kiln's typed tools and none of Pi's built-in mutation tools

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ REOPENED 2026-09-14 (F114): EVERY RESULT WAS STRUCTURED FOR KILN AND EMPTY FOR THE MODEL. EVD-0102 observed handler results returned through a recording stub and the session registry, not the provider-facing tool content. No wrapper result or refusal was model-visible. `rendered()` in `pi-package/extensions/kiln.js` returned `{output, details}` with no `content`, and Pi sends a tool result without `content` to the provider as `(no tool output)`. A real `/kiln-start` session measured it on 2026-09-14: `kiln_project_status` executed without error and the provider received exactly that placeholder. The historical evidence and its link are kept unchanged. This criterion returns to pass only on supplemental evidence that the provider-facing tool message carries the rendered result. ⚠️ RESTORED TO PASS 2026-09-14 ON EVD-0106: commit 81f69a9 returns every result as text content equal to its rendering, and CI run 34812083727 observed it at the handler boundary for all 28 tools and in a real provider request for kiln_capability. ⚠️ NARROWED TO TSK-0044. This criterion accepted TSK-0044 AND TSK-0045, which do not depend on each other, so neither could be finished without the other's work also being done - and its wording is about mutation wrappers, which are TSK-0044's, while TSK-0045's adapters mostly write no planning content at all. TSK-0045 now has its own criterion for what its adapters must do. ⚠️ THE WRAPPER IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION. Everything it calls already exists in `lib/` with the lock, the atomic write, the schema validation and the id allocator behind it. A wrapper that re-derived the content root, or re-checked a rule, would be a second answer to a question that already has one - which is how the two drift apart without either being obviously wrong.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each registered creation, mutation, activation and stage-attestation tool performs its write through the existing locked, atomic, validated implementation rather than reaching the filesystem itself, and every wrapper - read or write - resolves the content root through the shared resolver rather than deriving one. A wrapper adds only the Pi-facing schema and the rendering of a result: no validation rule, no id allocation, no trace rule and no write path is restated in it. Every result is structured, a refusal is returned as data rather than thrown as prose, and neither carries a credential, a credential-derived value or an absolute user path.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every registered wrapper writes through the existing discipline and adds nothing to it

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ SCOPED 2026-09-13 TO WHAT TSK-0046 PROMISES, AND NO FURTHER (O1, then F88). The criterion accepts the decision owner, the outputs and the exit criteria - the three things a canonical definition carries - together with the nine identities and their paths, byte determinism, the three drift classes by name, a check that writes nothing, and both CI platforms. Purpose, method, next activity, delegations, boundaries and the completion summary are accepted by ACC-0112 instead, because their canonical fields do not exist yet. ⚠️ OUTPUT PROSE IS NOT A PURPOSE (F88). `producesProse` says what a stage emits. A skill that printed it under Purpose would tell an agent what the stage is for on the strength of a field that never said so - the drift CMP-0033 exists to prevent, arrived at by relabelling rather than by duplication. ⚠️ MISSING AND ORPHANED ARE STALENESS TOO. A definition added without regenerating, and a definition removed while its skill stays packaged, are the same drift as an edited one; a check that only compared the files present on both sides would pass both. ⚠️ BYTE DETERMINISM IS WHAT MAKES THE CHECK MEAN ANYTHING. A generator whose output varies with line endings, key order or the clock makes every check stale on some platform, and a check that is always stale is one nobody reads.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The generator produces exactly nine packaged stage skills, one per canonical stage definition - `kiln-stage-01-intake`, `kiln-stage-02-intent-decomposition`, `kiln-stage-03-discovery`, `kiln-stage-04-requirement-gaps`, `kiln-stage-05-solution-design`, `kiln-stage-06-risk-feasibility`, `kiln-stage-07-acceptance-criteria`, `kiln-stage-08-implementation-plan`, `kiln-stage-09-handoff` - each at `pi-package/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with that name in its frontmatter, and each carrying its definition's decision owner, its outputs - the typed artifacts, the outputs not yet typed and the output prose - and its exit criteria. The output prose is rendered as output prose and never relabelled as the stage's purpose. Generation is deterministic: the same definitions produce byte-identical files on every run and on every platform, with no timestamp and no machine-specific content. The check mode writes nothing, and fails naming each skill by name that is stale (its content differs from what the definitions generate), missing (a definition has no generated skill) or orphaned (a generated skill has no definition). The check runs in CI on Windows and on Ubuntu. The handwritten `kiln-planning` skill is neither adopted nor removed by generation or by the check.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Packaged skills are generated, and staleness fails a check

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (F91, F92). The criterion said the override directory was registered after the packaged set, and it named three states. Pi 0.84.4 resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources and keeps the first skill with each name, and TSK-0047 promises four states; the packaged-only state and the exact meaning of removal - the skill removed, the directory and the entry kept - are now stated, with one generated identity and path-based provenance. ⚠️ CONTROLS, RECORDED AS BEHAVIOUR (D9). An absent override directory is silently ignored: Pi skips a settings skill path that does not exist, emits no diagnostic, and the packaged skill loads. An untrusted project - no trust decision, or an explicit denial - loads neither the package's resources nor the override, because Pi empties project settings when the project is not trusted. Neither control is a Kiln refusal. ⚠️ R8, NOT CLAIMED. Kiln's settings merge keeps every existing project `skills` entry where it is and appends its own. Project-settings entries share Pi's precedence and keep their order, so an earlier project-settings skill path holding the same identity outranks Kiln's appended override entry. This criterion does not claim otherwise. ⚠️ R9 IS SETUP'S (TSK-0060). The entry is fixed relative to `.pi`; that it names the selected content root's `skills-overrides/` is for setup to guarantee. This criterion proves the entry in the default layout, where the content root is `<project>/planning-content`.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: In an isolated trusted project whose `.pi/settings.json` holds Kiln's package entry and the skill-override entry `../planning-content/skills-overrides` as produced by `mergeSettingsText`, the pinned Pi runtime's real resource loader, reloaded for each state, resolves the generated skill identity `kiln-stage-01-intake` exactly as follows. (1) Packaged only - the override directory exists and holds no skill: the loaded skill's `filePath` is the packaged `pi-package/skills/kiln-stage-01-intake/SKILL.md`, and Pi reports no collision for that identity. (2) Override present - `planning-content/skills-overrides/kiln-stage-01-intake/SKILL.md` declares that name: exactly one skill with that identity loads, its `filePath` is the override file, and Pi's collision diagnostic names the override file as the winner path and the packaged file as the loser path. (3) Override edited - the override's description is changed: the same override `filePath` loads, with the edited description. (4) Override skill removed while the override directory and the settings entry remain: the packaged `filePath` and the packaged description load again, and Pi reports no collision for that identity. In every state the other packaged skills still load from the package. Provenance is read from `filePath` and the collision diagnostic's winner and loser paths, never from model behaviour. Pi 0.84.4 resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources, and the first skill loaded with a given identity wins, so this criterion claims only that the consumer override wins over the packaged skill, not over every earlier project-settings skill path.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A consumer override of a generated stage skill wins over the packaged skill, tracks edits, and reverts when removed

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-09-13 (F98, D14). The criterion used to accept that the first turn asked 'a single relevant question' and proposed no solution. Whether a question is relevant is model behaviour, and a scripted provider decides the answer before the model is asked, so a test built on one would claim a selection nobody made. This criterion now accepts only what Kiln deterministically gives the session. The user-visible first turn - a real model on a clean consumer - is accepted by the TSK-0063 journey criterion instead. ⚠️ PERSISTENCE MOVED (D15). Writing the operator's answer into the intake document is TSK-0049's continuous capture and has its own criterion there; no typed stage-document writer exists yet. ⚠️ FRESH IS DEFINED BY STATE, NOT BY TEXT (D12). No typed planning artifacts and no stage attestations. The generated starter documents and `project.yaml` exist in every initialised project and do not make it non-fresh. ⚠️ PASSED 2026-09-14 ON EVD-0107: G4 run 34790900443 and G5 run 34838944777 observed the hook, the status tool and a real trusted /kiln-start session at the provider, with the packaged and the edited-override skill. Declared: R10, R12, F82, local-only mutations, no macOS.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: On a fresh project - one with no typed planning artifacts and no stage attestations, whatever its starter documents and project metadata say - `/kiln-start` deterministically supplies the orchestrator with the project's name and description and the Stage 1 starter document, both through `kiln_project_status`; the exact loaded `kiln-stage-01-intake` skill content, injected at `before_agent_start` from the derived current stage, including a consumer override when Pi resolved one; and instructions to ask exactly one question, to propose no architecture, requirement set or solution, and to call no mutating tool. Each of these is observed in what the session is given, not inferred from what a model says.
acceptanceCriteria.title: On a fresh project, /kiln-start supplies Stage 1's context and one-question instructions

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Evidence split agreed 2026-09-18 during TSK-0049. This criterion stays a claim about model behaviour: the second question itself must differ, not merely the state it is derived from. Restating it as "the state turn two is derived from differs" was considered and refused, because that is the mechanism and not adaptive questioning. It is therefore evidenced in two parts, and neither part alone satisfies it. (1) Deterministic tests prove the mechanism: two different first answers produce different persisted intake state and different turn-two inputs, with no real model involved. (2) Two retained real-model runs prove the behaviour: both start from the same project snapshot, differ only in the operator's first answer, and are reviewed by a person for whether the second questions differ and are relevant to the answers given.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: After the intake document changes, the next question differs according to what the answer supplied — demonstrated by driving two different first answers from the same starting state and observing two different second questions.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The second question is chosen from updated state, not from a list

acceptanceCriteria.notes:
Amended 2026-09-18 under TSK-0050, before implementation, and again the same day (F18). The original statement named Stage 1 attestation alone. The boundary is the same act for artifact approval and for type activation and deactivation, so all three are stated here rather than left to the implementation to generalise. Material-change preview is a separate criterion, ACC-0115: that one is the orchestrator's behaviour before a mutation, where this one is the tool boundary that holds whatever the orchestrator does.

Authorisation is Pi's interactive confirmation channel, `ctx.ui.confirm`, called with the invocation's own signal and a 30,000 ms timeout. Only a literal `true` authorises the action. No UI context, rejection, cancellation, timeout, abort and an unexpected UI error all refuse and all write the bounded refusal record. They share one refusal code, `operator-confirmation-not-granted`, because Pi returns the same `false` for every one of them: with no UI bound `confirm` is `async () => false`, and in RPC mode a cancelled dialog and an expired timeout both resolve `false` through the same path, which is why the SDK's own timed-confirm example labels the result "Cancelled or timed out". A code claiming to separate them would be a distinction Kiln invented rather than observed. An unexpected UI error refuses without the raw error reaching the model or the record.

F18: what each operation DOES with Kiln's actor string differs, and this criterion claims only what is true of all three. All three receive `operator via Pi UI`. Attestation persists it as `decidedBy`, and activation persists it in the project manifest. Review status persists the `approved` status and returns the actor to the caller, but stores no approver: the artifact envelope in `schemas/common.schema.json` has no reviewer field. Adding one, or an approval history, is an artifact-schema and migration decision that TSK-0050 does not make, so neither this criterion nor the confirmation dialog claims durable attribution for an approval.

The refusal record is `state/operator-boundary-refusals.json`, bounded at the newest 100 entries and holding only validated identifiers and enums. Evidence is split: deterministic tests cover both the confirmed and the refused branch, including an injected UI context for the confirmed one, because a harness that answered the dialog would be acting as the operator. The retained RPC run leaves the dialog unanswered and shows refusal after the bound.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: An attempt by the orchestrator to attest or advance a stage exit criterion, to set an artifact's review status to `approved`, or to activate or deactivate an artifact type is refused unless the operator confirmed that exact action through Kiln's interactive confirmation channel during that same tool invocation. No model-supplied argument can carry an authorisation value or actor identity. After confirmation, Kiln supplies its own internal actor string to the underlying operation; any actor identity that operation records therefore comes from Kiln, not the model. The confirmation result does not outlive the invocation that obtained it. Where no confirmation channel is available, or the operator cancels, rejects, or does not answer, the tool refuses with a stable refusal code. On a refusal the target attestation file, artifact file and type manifest are unchanged in bytes and in modification time, and a bounded refusal record naming the operation, the refusal code and the target identifiers is persisted and reported by `kiln_project_status`.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The orchestrator cannot cross a user-owned gate

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-09-13 (F96, F97, D13). F96: the launcher refuses the tool checkout (`resolveSelfHost`, EVD-0089), but the orchestrator's handlers re-resolve the content root inside the Pi child, which inherits `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR`, and `resolveContentRoot` accepts any override - including the tool's own `planning-content/` - because its inside-the-tool-root backstop runs only without one. The child is never told whether self-hosting was validated, and Pi started without the launcher bypasses the launcher's refusal entirely. So the refusal must also live in the orchestrator, gated by a marker only the launcher emits. F97: 'names both paths' conflicted with the model-facing disclosure boundary - tool results expose no absolute path - so the operator sees canonical paths and the model sees placeholders. ⚠️ STRICT MEANS STRICT. A marker that accepted 'true', '1' or an empty value would let any inherited environment variable grant self-hosting; only the exact value the launcher writes after validation permits it. ⚠️ PASSED 2026-09-14 ON EVD-0108: G3b run 34778806796 observed the resolver, every handler's two refusal surfaces and the supervisor's marker propagation. acceptanceCriteria.statement: Started in a consumer checkout, the orchestrator resolves the canonical sibling content root. In any state in which the tool's own bundled planning content would resolve instead - including `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR` naming it, and a sibling that is a link into it - it refuses before authoring anything, and no file under either root changes. The refusal has two surfaces: the operator-facing refusal names both canonical absolute paths, the resolved content root and the tool root; the model-facing structured refusal carries a stable refusal code and stable placeholders for those paths, and no absolute path. Self-hosting is permitted only by an explicit, strict self-host marker that the launcher emits into the orchestrator's environment after it has validated `--self-host`; an absent marker, or any value other than the exact expected one, refuses.
acceptanceCriteria.title: It refuses to operate on the tool's own planning content

The verifier's field and its refusal reason describe task binding rather than stdin.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Stdin is closed and the exact task still arrived

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A child that exits zero, emits a well-formed transcript and returns plausible prose without Kiln's tools causes the delegation to fail loudly; none of its substantive output is used. The same holds for signature drift, an out-of-role write, a nonzero exit, a timeout, malformed JSON events, a missing task binding and a provider or model mismatch.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A child without the Kiln capability signature is refused, not read
