acceptanceCriteria.title: The child inherits the orchestrator's exact selection and a scoped context

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Two proofs are required together, because either alone passes in the arrangement this criterion forbids. Structurally: under the supervisor the application launcher is spawned with a private stdin the supervisor can WRITE to and CLOSE, while Pi is spawned with the terminal inherited. Behaviourally: with a launcher-side reader actively attempting to consume input, an exact sentinel written to the supervisor's own stdin is received by Pi and the launcher-side reader receives none of that sentinel — it is expected to receive the supervisor's later stop control message, which is its own channel working. A positive check that input reached Pi does not satisfy this on its own: it passes whenever Pi happens to win a read, including when both processes hold the terminal, which is precisely the defect. The control must fail when the launcher's stdin is changed from a private pipe to inherited terminal input, and a control that survives that mutation has not tested this criterion. The launcher continues to stop on the stop control message and on its stdin being closed. ⚠️ SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE: the harness supplies a pipe rather than a pseudo-terminal, so what is proved is descriptor ownership and byte routing, not terminal line discipline or signal behaviour. The structural assertion is what ties it to the real topology — whatever descriptor 0 is, the launcher is not given it.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The background launcher cannot read the terminal, proved against an adversary

acceptanceCriteria.statement: With an unrelated server already answering on the chosen port, launch refuses rather than reporting the browser ready. A response carrying a wrong run identifier, a wrong project identifier, or arriving while the expected child is not alive, likewise fails readiness.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An unrelated healthy HTTP service does not satisfy readiness

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A port outside 1..65535 or a non-integer value is refused. When the default is occupied, interactive mode offers another available port for that invocation only and non-interactive mode refuses with an exact PORT recovery command. An automatically chosen port is never written into project configuration.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Port handling refuses out-of-range values and never silently persists a choice

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ Reopened 2026-09-15 on R18 and R19; settled 2026-09-16. EVD-0088 stands unchanged as the historical record of commit 36df281. R18 was a real overrun and a criterion/evidence mismatch: run 34910936533 recorded spentMs 8092 against an 8,000 ms budget with withinBudget false, while the evidence test passed it against an unstated 9,500 ms ceiling, the budget plus six 250 ms phase floors. Identity reads and termination spawns ran outside every scaled wait, so neither the budget nor that ceiling bounded them. Both are closed: one deadline now covers every operation, that ceiling is deleted, and a completed result requires withinBudget. R19 is closed by a per-operation timeline that records when each tree was observed stopped. The 8,000 ms budget is unchanged; what changed is that it is enforced rather than described. F119, intermittent Windows WMI latency, is MITIGATED, NOT ELIMINATED: the provider's first use is now paid by the bounded launch preflight, measured at 3,142 ms and 3,057 ms on cold CI runners, after which every tracked query cost 370 to 830 ms. If a primed route times out again in CI, WMI is removed wholesale in favour of a WMI-free identity format, which is a deliberate change of identity precision and not a fallback. F119's successor is settled: F122 retired WMI after a primed timeout, and EVD-0111 records the WMI-free reader, the six complete Windows records under the enforced deadline, and F130 as instrumented but unexplained. ⚠️ FAIL 2026-09-24 on EVD-0146. After an interrupt on a loaded Windows runner (CI run 36074016941, job 107881093769), the launcher's identity read ran out of deadline. A launcher descendant was still running when the supervisor returned. The shutdown was correctly reported partial (launcher-descendants-unverified), but both trees were not stopped, and this criterion requires that they were. O1 (ca476de) fixed the natural-mode starvation and is verified for natural shutdown only. The pass is not restored until both open mechanisms are resolved: the live descendant after an interrupt, and the short-lived agent whose descendants the tracker never observes (F130, TSK-0058). ✅ PASS 2026-09-25 on EVD-0149, against the statement as amended the same day (29f529d, eb9df03). Both F130 mechanisms are resolved: on Windows both trees start in jobs, so a short-lived agent's descendants and a launcher descendant after an interrupt are named and ended by their jobs, and one Ctrl+C in an interactive session is a keyboard stop. The overall CI run carrying the evidence was red on one Windows Node 22 cell, where the journey test's headless Chrome never exposed a page after Kiln's first run had passed its shutdown checks; the cause was not captured and nothing observed ties it to Kiln, disclosed in EVD-0149. ⚠️ FAIL 2026-09-25, reopened the same day. The shipped command recorded budget.ms 11000 (EVD-0150: the supervisor defaults of 8,000 ms grace plus 3,000 ms hard), while this criterion states one 8,000 ms deadline and its evidence fixture ran with 5,000 plus 3,000. EVD-0149 evidenced the fixture configuration, not the shipped one. The criterion stands; the product is corrected to one shared 5,000 plus 3,000 configuration used by the command and the fixture, and this pass is not restored until the real command records budget.ms 8000 and CI passes. ✅ PASS RESTORED 2026-09-25 on EVD-0152 with EVD-0149: the shipped command records the stated 8,000 ms budget from the one configuration its evidence also uses, the per-tree stop functions default to it too, and CI run 36196549020 passed all four cells with every evidence record at budget.ms 8000.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: After Pi exits, after an interrupt, or after one Ctrl+C at the keyboard in an interactive Kiln session, both process trees are stopped within their grace periods, the port is free, and only files created by that invocation were removed. Seven things are observed and recorded SEPARATELY, because they fail separately and because any one of them standing for the others is how a shutdown claim becomes untestable. An observation that was not made is recorded as unmade and the shutdown is reported partial; it is never treated as one that passed. (1) Which of the three triggers ended the run — Pi exiting on its own, a signal, or the keyboard stop — each recorded where it was observed rather than supplied beside it, so the record cannot contradict itself. A signal is recorded where it was handled and never inferred from the processes having gone. The keyboard stop exists because an interactive Pi reads Ctrl+C as a key, so no signal occurs: Kiln's Pi extension consumes the key in the editor and in dialogs and writes a per-run notice before asking Pi to stop, and the stop is recorded as `keyboard` when the supervisor sees that notice, including when Pi's exit is observed first; it never records a signal that did not occur. A run ended by Pi exiting on its own records neither a signal nor a keyboard stop. (2) For each tree independently, either that it had already exited or that a stop was requested of it: a tree that was already gone is recorded as such and is not asked, and a supervisor that asks one tree and not the other looks identical to a correct one on every run where the unasked tree exits anyway. (3) That each tree's exit was independently observed, so one going never stands in for the other. (4) That where a graceful stop did not complete, escalation was bounded and its outcome observed — reported as unobserved rather than assumed when the process still did not go. (5) That the port accepts a fresh exclusive bind afterwards, observed by rebinding rather than derived from any process record: an exit code says the leader is gone and says nothing about a worker still listening. (6) That only runtime files this invocation created were removed, proved by a file it did not create still being present afterwards, not merely by its own being gone. (7) That the results are recorded independently for Windows and for the supported POSIX platform through CI, rather than one platform's pass standing for both, and that each platform's observation includes a KNOWN DESCENDANT of each tree rather than only the leader's exit code. The platforms differ in the only mechanism that matters here: a graceful signal is unavailable on Windows, and on POSIX a process group can be targeted only for a child spawned as a group leader — which the foreground agent cannot be, since a detached process cannot read the terminal, so its descendants must be enumerated and signalled individually. A descendant enumeration that fails is recorded as unmade, because an empty list would claim a tree with no children. On Windows both trees are held by jobs (the launch prerequisite below), so each tree's descendants are its job's members, listed and terminated through the job, and a job that cannot be listed is recorded as unmade in the same way. Two bounds are stated separately, because they cover different work and are paid at different times. THE WINDOWS LAUNCH PREREQUISITE: Pi and the launcher are each created suspended inside a job object held by a host process outside that job, with kill-on-job-close set, and each is resumed only once it is assigned, so every descendant, detached ones included, is a member of its tree's job from its first instruction. A host that cannot create the job, set its limits, create the process or assign it refuses the launch, and nothing falls back to a plain spawn or to process-table tracking. No Windows shutdown operation then reads a process table, so the process-table preflight is not run on Windows and is recorded as not run, with that reason. The hosts' start-up is the launch's own cost and is never counted against the shutdown budget. POSIX has neither job hosts nor a preflight. THE SHUTDOWN: from the trigger — Pi exiting, an interrupt arriving, or the keyboard stop's notice being seen, without waiting for Pi to exit — the whole teardown has one 8,000 ms deadline, and every operation draws its allowance from it: the descendant tracker joins, each tree's grace and hard waits, every identity read, every signal or `taskkill`, the launcher's control channel, the removal of this invocation's owned files, and the port probe. An operation whose minimum allowance the deadline cannot cover is not started, is named in the record's `unfinished` list with its reason, and makes the result incomplete. A shutdown is complete only when all six hold: both trees were observed stopped; the port accepts a fresh exclusive bind; the removal of owned files succeeded; every required observation was made, so `notObserved` is empty; `unfinished` is empty; and `withinBudget` is true. A teardown that ran past its deadline is not complete, whatever else it managed.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Shutdown leaves nothing running on either platform

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Run where the tool root and project root are the same directory, the normal command refuses rather than writing `.pi/` into the tool repository. acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE IMMEDIATE-QUIT RUN EXISTS BECAUSE OF F82 (2026-09-12), AND IT IS THE ONE CELL NOTHING ELSE CAN OBSERVE. WHAT WAS MEASURED: over 98 runs against the pinned runtime on Windows, `--mode rpc` on Node 24.18.0 aborts with a libuv assertion - `Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94`, exit 3221226505 (0xC0000409) - when shutdown begins within 50ms of a SECOND OR LATER turn settling. WHAT WAS NOT THE CAUSE: it is not tool execution. A tool call forces a second provider request, and two text-only turns abort identically; one turn never does. Forcing a fresh connection per request and disabling session persistence each still abort. THE CONTROLS WERE CLEAN: Node 22.23.2 in every configuration, print mode with and without a tool call, terminating the child rather than asking it to stop, and every shutdown delayed 50ms or more. WHY IT IS NOT A TASK: Kiln's launch never passes `--mode`, so production runs interactive or, without a TTY, print - and print was clean. No Kiln code is on that stack, and no delay, flag or dependency patch is justified by evidence that does not reach production. THE INTERACTIVE PATH, OBSERVED 2026-09-25 (EVD-0151). It ends in the same `process.exit(0)` as RPC, with an awaited terminal drain in front of it. It was observed in Windows Terminal on Node 24.18.0, where Pi had a real console on both ends and ran interactive: a second turn completed a tool call, and `/quit` was submitted 9 ms and 44 ms after Pi's own `agent_end`, inside the 50 ms window. The keystrokes were synthetic input events sent to a Windows Terminal window verified to be in the foreground, not a physical keypress, and a person reviewed the retained records against their hashes. Both runs exited 0 through the supervisor with a complete shutdown, no surviving tree, no bound port and no run file left. IF IT FAILS: a dedicated defect and an upstream report are opened before this criterion is accepted. A delay is a diagnostic control and is not a fix. ✅ PASS 2026-09-25 on EVD-0151 (the immediate quit after a completed tool call on a second turn, Windows and Node 24) and EVD-0145 (clean shutdown, exact resume and unchanged setup in the documented journey). EVD-0150 is linked as the earlier first-turn runs, which did not meet the second-turn condition. LIMIT: the keys were synthetic input in a verified foreground Windows Terminal window; no physical keypress is claimed.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Stopping the supervisor leaves no child process, no bound port and no temporary file from that invocation; rerunning resumes the recorded session and the current stage, and the setup phase changes no bytes. One of the runs is a real interactive session on Windows and Node 24 quit immediately after a completed tool call: it exits cleanly through the supervisor, its process exit status and the supervisor's shutdown record are retained, and it leaves no child, no bound port and no temporary file of that invocation behind.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Shutdown is clean and a rerun resumes rather than restarting

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-09-03. It now records what Pi does; what Kiln must do about it is a separate criterion downstream of the setup command. ⚠️ 'STATED AS THE OBSERVED OUTCOME, NOT A REQUIRED ONE' is the load-bearing phrase: an observation that only passes when the runtime behaves the way the design hoped is not an observation. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-21 (F7, F8): Pi 0.84.4 has no authentication-only launch, so the observation is of the full interactive TUI with /login typed into it, and the no-TTY runs are recorded as the print-mode runs they are. ✅ PASS 2026-09-21 on EVD-0123. Pi 0.84.4 has no authentication-only launch, so the full interactive TUI was observed owning the terminal while /login saved an OpenAI API key, and a separate pi auth check --no-refresh went from not_ready to ready. With stdin or stdout not a TTY the TUI never rendered: two runs exited 0 silently and two were still running at the 20 s timeout, and none refused. The auth check proves local configuration, not a working provider key; account authentication is TSK-0066.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A manually invoked check records, against the pinned runtime alone: that the full interactive Pi TUI, launched against an isolated Pi configuration, owns the terminal while `/login` completes through the built-in `openai` API-key route with a throwaway key; that its exit is distinguished from configured authentication by a separate `pi auth check --provider openai --json --no-refresh` afterwards, which confirms locally configured authentication and does not prove the key works against a provider; and, with the same arguments and stdin, stdout or both not a TTY, which mode Pi selected and the bounded outcome (exit and code, error, or still running at a stated timeout), stated as observed rather than as required. Those controls are not the interactive mode and are not described as it. A sanitized transcript is retained, and the entered key is not recorded. No claim is made here about Kiln's refusal or recovery messaging, about OAuth, or about usable account authentication.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Pi's interactive /login is observed owning the terminal, and the no-TTY controls are recorded

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE SECOND HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL. A model appearing in `getAvailable()` after a login is consistent with the login having worked and equally consistent with it having been available already; only the revocation distinguishes them. ⚠️ THE 'FRESHLY CONSTRUCTED' CLAUSE MATTERS TOO: reusing a runtime built before the login would report a cached snapshot, and 'login UI exited' is not 'login succeeded' — the same rule section 6.2 applies to the exit code. ⚠️ FABRICATION IS EXCLUDED IN THE STATEMENT RATHER THAN IN A NOTE, because it is the cheap way to make this pass and it would prove a storage shape instead of usable authentication. ✅ PASS 2026-09-21 on EVD-0124. One manual, account-bound Windows run with an isolated Pi configuration and a sanitized environment: after a real /login to openai-codex, a freshly constructed ModelRuntime and ModelRegistry reported gpt-5.5 in getAvailable() with hasConfiguredAuth() true, and after the stored credential was removed the same construction reported it unavailable. The record is sanitized and labelled manual, account-bound and single-instance, and no fabricated credential was used. CI run 35644573627 passed the retained test in all four cells. LIMITS: this is registry discovery and its loss. No model request or token refresh was made, removal was local rather than a provider-side revocation, and nothing is inferred for other providers or for Linux.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A manual run against a real subscription records, with an isolated Pi configuration directory and a sanitized environment: that after Pi's interactive `/login` exits, a FRESHLY constructed `ModelRuntime` and `ModelRegistry` report the chosen built-in model in `getAvailable()` and return true from `hasConfiguredAuth()`; and that after the stored credential is removed or revoked, the same construction reports the model unavailable. The retained record is sanitized — asserted to contain no token, authorisation header, credential-derived value, username or absolute home path — and is labelled manual, account-bound and single-instance. A fabricated OAuth credential does not satisfy this criterion in any form.
acceptanceCriteria.title: OAuth is proved by a real login and its revocation, or it is not called verified

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-21 on EVD-0106 and EVD-0122. Presence: a real loaded session calls kiln_capability and receives the shipped declaration (EVD-0106). Drift: real sessions on Windows and Linux, Pi 0.84.4, read every research tool signature from the live registry, and verifyChild accepts the unmodified package and refuses a changed research_fetch as signature-mismatch without returning its output (EVD-0122). CI run 35591168378 at d927151 passed in all four cells, and the live tier re-proved it on ubuntu-latest node 24 only. LIMIT: verifyChild compares property names and the required list only, so a type-only change is not detected and this criterion does not cover one.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Once the Kiln package exists, a real Pi run reports its capability signature in the loaded session, and a deliberate change to a measured tool signature causes a comparing consumer to refuse. Both halves are required: presence alone does not show that a consumer would notice its absence.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The capability signature is observed in a loaded session, and drift is detected

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ THE PROCESS-NEVER-SPAWNED HALF IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A refusal message printed just before launching the TUI anyway would satisfy a text assertion and still hang a CI job, which is the failure this exists to prevent — a hang is indistinguishable from work until a timeout. ⚠️ AND THE SECOND ROW IS A CONTROL: if the non-TTY path refused unconditionally, the refusal would prove nothing about TTY detection. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-21 (F8): stdout is checked as well as stdin, because Pi itself leaves interactive mode when either is not a TTY. ✅ PASS 2026-09-26 on EVD-0153: in each no-terminal case the stand-in launch function was never called and setup exited 18 naming both routes; the real piped command confirmed exit 18 and the recovery text; with authentication present the same run proceeded.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: With stdin, stdout or both not a TTY and no usable authentication already present, setup refuses BEFORE starting the interactive Pi TUI — verified by the Pi process never being spawned, not merely by the message printed — and prints both supported recovery routes: run setup from a local interactive terminal, or configure authentication on the target host outside Kiln and rerun with the required non-interactive decisions. Each of the three non-TTY combinations is checked. With usable authentication already present, the same non-TTY invocation proceeds instead of refusing.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Setup refuses before launching login when there is no terminal, and names the way out

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-03, mechanised in `test/link-trace.test.mjs`. Each repair case asserts BOTH that the link is gone and that the lint finding it produced has cleared — `trace/wrong-target-type` for a wrong-type target, `trace/target-missing` for a deleted one, `lifecycle/trace-to-inactive` for a superseded one — because 'the array is shorter' was never the claim; 'the graph is repaired' is. Each fixture first asserts the finding EXISTS, so a case that stopped producing damage could not pass by repairing nothing. ⚠️ THE FIX IS AN ASYMMETRY AND BOTH HALVES ARE TESTED IN THE SAME FILE. Removal now inspects nothing about the target; addition still refuses a wrong type, a dangling reference and a malformed id. A later simplification that made them share one validation path would repair nothing and would pass a file that only tested removal. ⚠️ `answeredBy` OPENED FOR REMOVAL ONLY, and it is the only field that did. `supportedBy` and `refutedBy` still route to `unlinkEvidence` and `supersededBy` to `setLifecycle`, because those removal operations genuinely exist; `answeredBy` had none, which is what forced the deliberate exploitation of the companion defect during Phase 1. Adding an answer link still routes through `resolveQuestion`. ⚠️ THE WRITE DISCIPLINE IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the fresh-read-inside-the-lock is proved by editing the file between the artifact's creation and the unlink and requiring the edit to survive; the atomic write by requiring no temporary file beside the artifact; and the lock by requiring it released. #16's amend-on-change is covered, including that a no-op does not amend.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: `unlinkTrace` removes a link whose target is of the wrong type, whose target does not exist, and whose target has been superseded — each verified by the link being gone and the lint finding it clears. It removes `answeredBy` entries, which no operation could previously withdraw. It continues to refuse an unknown FIELD, and it preserves the lock, fresh-read and atomic-write discipline. Adding a link is unaffected and still validates the target type.
acceptanceCriteria.title: An invalid or stale link can be removed through the typed path

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-03. The guard is now `Array.isArray(effectiveSchema(schemas, type).properties[k]['x-traceTarget'])`, asked PER TYPE rather than as a union, because a name that is a link on one type need not be one on another. It is the same source `linkTrace` validates against, so the two cannot drift. ⚠️ THE COUNT WAS EIGHT, NOT NINE, AND MY EARLIER ACCOUNTS OF THIS DEFECT SAID NINE. They included `implementedBy`, which is deliberately NOT a trace field — the component schema says so explicitly: 'Paths rather than a trace field on purpose: code is not an artifact, and pretending it is would put the repository inside the planning model.' It declares no `x-traceTarget`, the derived guard leaves it alone, and a test asserts that it stays revisable. Enumerating from the schemas is what surfaced the miscount; a hand-written list would have carried it. ⚠️ THE SCHEMAS DECLARE 25 TRACE FIELDS AND THE OLD LIST HELD 17. Every name in the old list was a real trace field, so the defect was never a wrong entry — it was the eight that were never added, which is the failure mode of any guard maintained by hand beside a declaration that already exists. `reviseArtifact` already resolved the effective schema a few lines later, for materiality, under a comment reading 'never from a hardcoded field list'. The rule was in the file; it just had not been applied to the guard above it.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: `reviseArtifact` refuses every field the schemas declare with `x-traceTarget`, established by enumerating those fields from the schema set at test time and asserting a refusal for each — not by comparing against a second list written in the test. Adding a trace field to a schema therefore extends the guard with no code change, proved by introducing one in a copied schema set and requiring the refusal. The eight fields that were previously reachable — `acceptedBy`, `answeredBy`, `blocks`, `evaluates`, `fulfils`, `raisedBy`, `satisfies` and `verifies` — are refused, while a non-trace field on the same type stays revisable so the guard is discriminating rather than simply refusing everything.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The trace-field guard is derived from the schemas, and covers every declared trace field

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every file the transaction may write is resolved through its deepest existing ancestor and proved to lie beneath a root the caller explicitly authorised, and the same proof is repeated under the lock immediately before each write. A junction or symbolic link on a target's path refuses and nothing is written through it, including a probe, even when the path spells as one inside the project. A root the caller did not pass is not a root the transaction can write to, and the transaction lock is not a writable target. Each target's plan key is derived from its resolved path, so two entries that reach the same physical file refuse whether they differ only in spelling or arrive through two authorised roots that overlap, and one file merged under any of its spellings reaches the single entry planned for it.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every write target is identified by resolution, not by spelling

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The write plan is built while this process demonstrably holds the transaction lock, and planning refuses when it is not held. A plan that refuses leaves the project as it was found, directories included: every probe file and every directory created in order to probe is removed on every exit path. Where a removal cannot be completed, the transaction refuses and names each path it left behind, retaining alongside it whatever refusal caused the attempt — a cleanup failure is never reported as success. Absence is confirmed by observing the path, not by trusting the removal call's error code.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Planning holds the lock, and a refused plan leaves the project unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When the content a merge would produce is byte-identical to what is already on disk, the transaction performs no write. The evidence is the file's modification time, not the merge's reported status.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A merge that would produce the current bytes writes nothing

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The journal is a planned, contained target validated against its schema before each write, and it records the whole ordered phase plan up front, marking a phase running before that phase's work begins. On failure it survives, naming the last completed phase and an exact recovery command, and nothing already written is rolled back. On success it is deleted, and a deletion that fails for any reason other than the file already being absent is reported rather than swallowed.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The journal is a planned target whose lifecycle is never silent

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given a transaction that already holds the project lock, the initializer runs inside it and produces content byte-identical to a standalone run, with the marked ignore block appended at most once and every pre-existing line intact; a second run inside a held transaction still reports already-initialised and does not touch the ignore file. The transaction is accepted only as an authenticated, currently live capability: an object carrying the right shape but not issued by the transaction module is refused, a genuine transaction whose run has finished is refused, and one holding a different project is refused — each without writing anything. Work runs inside a transaction only by being registered with it, so a collaborator authenticated at entry is also enrolled for its duration rather than left to run beside it. A transaction is revoked before its lock is released and every operation through a revoked transaction is refused. In-flight work is drained to quiescence before revocation, including work started by work already being drained, so nothing registered with the transaction is still running when the lock is released. Where any work was still running at the moment the body returned, that work completes under the lock and the run is reported failed. No claim is made about operations the body did not await which had already settled: they are indistinguishable from awaited ones and cannot cross the release boundary. An acquisition of a lock already held further up the same call stack is refused immediately rather than waiting out its bounded retry, that refusal expires with the lock so an acquisition from an async context descended from a released lock succeeds, and two concurrent independent acquisitions in one process still serialise.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The initializer runs inside an authenticated, live transaction

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Started with a run identifier and a project identifier, the launcher validates both before use and the application it starts answers its health endpoint with exactly those values — observed from the application's response, not from the launcher's own output, since a launcher printing an identifier proves only that it parsed one. The port is parsed rather than coerced, and a value that is not a whole number between 1 and 65535 is refused before anything is installed or built; an empty value is refused rather than treated as unset, because a supervisor whose port computation produced nothing would otherwise bind the default and then poll the port it believed it had chosen. A partial, malformed or present-but-empty identity is refused with the offending variable named and its value not echoed, never treated as a standalone run: standalone means the variables are absent, not blank, and starting anyway would produce a shell the supervisor can never recognise, reported to the operator as a readiness timeout two processes away from its cause. The launcher stops on the stop control message arriving on the stdin it was given, and stops equally on that stdin being closed with no message — a supervisor that dies cannot send anything, but the operating system closes its pipes regardless. Both paths terminate the child, remove the run directory, and free the port. The application is given no stdin at all, so it cannot read from the handle the launcher's own control channel arrives on. Interactive standalone operation — a terminal on stdin, no identity supplied — is unchanged, and the existing content-root refusal, single-child ownership and cleanup behaviour continue to hold. Standalone operation on a PIPED stdin is deliberately not unchanged: closing that pipe stops the launcher whether or not a supervisor is present, which is the intended behaviour rather than a preserved one. This criterion makes no claim about readiness: the launcher propagates an identity, and confirming that the process answering is the one this invocation started is the supervisor's to establish.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The launcher propagates a validated identity and stops through the stdin it is given

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When Pi exits, the supervisor sends the stop control message on the launcher's stdin, requests that stdin be ended, and then waits for the launcher to exit within a bounded period, escalating if it does not. Three facts are recorded separately: that the message was sent, that the end was requested, and whether the exit was actually observed. A run whose launcher was never seen to exit is reported as a failure with the address something may still be listening on — not as a success carrying the agent's own exit code, since the agent finishing cleanly says nothing about whether the launcher went. Writing to the pipe never throws: a stream error is delivered asynchronously, so it is listened for rather than wrapped in a try. An error observed before the shutdown result is finalised is recorded on that result; one arriving after it is not, and the criterion claims no more than that — what proves the launcher went is the observed exit, not the error record. That the launcher REACTS to a stop message and to a close is established elsewhere and is not what this asks; what this asks is that the supervisor performs the contract, since a supervisor that never sends anything is indistinguishable from one that does whenever the launcher would have exited for its own reasons. The wait is bounded in both directions: returning before the child is gone leaves a process holding the port, and waiting without limit replaces a hung application with a hung terminal. ⚠️ SIGNAL HANDLING, BOTH PROCESS TREES, GRACE PERIODS ACROSS PLATFORMS AND INVOCATION-OWNED FILE CLEANUP ARE NOT THIS CRITERION'S. They are ACC-0081's, on TSK-0058; claiming them here would mark work accepted that nothing has built.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The supervisor performs the Pi-exit handoff and observes the launcher go

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ REOPENED 2026-09-24. The pass on EVD-0110 did not cover the clause "On that first run the supervisor sends the start prompt". EVD-0110 measures session identity, resume and recovery, and its observations stand. No code sent a start prompt: a first run started Pi with its entry file, --tools, --provider, --model, --thinking and --session-id and no message (bin/start-kiln.mjs, lib/supervisor.mjs), and every test that reached /kiln-start sent it itself over RPC. This criterion is re-evaluated once the supervisor sends /kiln-start on a new session only and a real-command control observes it. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-24: the start prompt is required on a first INTERACTIVE run only. With piped input Pi runs in print mode and joins the piped text and a positional /kiln-start into one unexpanded message (EVD-0143), so a run whose input or output is not a terminal is sent no start prompt and its piped text is the first turn. Not re-evaluated until the four-cell CI run for the correction passes; EVD-0143 holds the local measurements. ⚠️ RE-EVALUATED 2026-09-24: PASS on EVD-0110 and EVD-0143. CI run 36038639205 at 009a16e passed all four cells; the real-command control ran and passed on both Ubuntu cells and is skipped on Windows, where the unit cases cover the argument list. A Windows interactive session is observed only by ACC-0088's manual run.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A fresh start requires BOTH that no session record is present and that the session storage was successfully inspected and found absent or empty. Storage that could not be inspected — unreadable, or a regular file where the directory belongs — is not an empty one, and a record that exists but cannot be opened is not a missing one: only a genuine absence answers, and every other failure asks. Starting fresh over sessions nobody could enumerate is the failure this clause exists to prevent, and it is reachable by exactly those two routes. On a first interactive run, where Pi's input and output are both terminals, the supervisor sends the start prompt; on every first run it records the session it began. On a later run it resumes the exact session named in the record, proved by the session identifier the agent was invoked with matching the stored one — not by the agent having started successfully, which is equally true of a brand-new unrelated session and is the check this criterion exists to rule out. The record is accepted only when its project and its state mode both match the run: a state root can be shared or copied, so a record whose every field is individually valid can still belong to another project, and the mode decides which store the identifier refers to. When the record is missing, unreadable, invalid, foreign, recorded under a different mode, or names a session that is no longer there, the supervisor presents the sessions actually available and asks; it never silently resumes a different one and never silently starts a fresh one in place of a session the operator believes they are returning to. A non-interactive run refuses instead, with the exact recovery command for the shell it is running in. The record names a session and a mode and carries no absolute path, so a project moved or a state root relocated does not resume something belonging elsewhere.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A rerun resumes the exact recorded session, not merely a session

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ AVAILABILITY AND `configured` DISAGREE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS MEASURED. The pinned runtime's `getProviderAuthStatus()` can report `configured: true` while `hasConfiguredAuth()` is false and the model is absent from `getAvailable()`; the compatibility spike's `withOAuth` cell records exactly that, with `statusDisagreesWithAvailability: true`. Anything gating on "some authentication source is configured" tells an operator they are connected when they cannot infer, which is why this criterion names the available-model set rather than the status object. ⚠️ THE PERMITTED CATEGORIES ARE THE THREE CMP-0029 DECLARES. Pi's own vocabulary is wider: `runtime` means a key was passed on the command line, and `models_json_command` and `fallback` are routes that produce a credential by executing something or by inheriting an extension's. None of the three is a category Kiln permits, so each is a refusal rather than a classification — mapping them onto `custom-environment-key` would let a route the table refuses arrive under a name it accepts. ⚠️ THE REPORT IS A CLOSED SHAPE, NOT A FILTERED ONE. Pi's `environment` status carries a `label` built from `getConfigValueEnvVarNames()` — variable NAMES — so a report assembled by spreading the status object leaks them by default. Asserting the absence of known-bad fields cannot see a field nobody thought of; asserting the exact key set can. ⚠️ WHAT THIS CANNOT REACH, and it is an evidence omission rather than a gap in the criterion: OAuth for a BUILT-IN provider needs an interactive `/login` against a real account. A `models.json` provider is composed with apiKey auth only, so a stored OAuth credential for one has no flow to resolve it — the spike records this as `oauthProvedForCustomProvider: false` and `oauthRemainsOpenForBuiltInProviders: true`. Real completions, token refresh and subscription-tier behaviour are account-bound for the same reason.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Before a provider contract is accepted, a disposable restricted child using the pinned Pi SDK resolves the exact selected provider and model. Availability comes from that exact model appearing in the available-model set, never merely from the provider reporting configured. A successful report contains only provider, model, availability and an auth-source category permitted by the declared contract. Planted credentials, variable names, headers and credential-derived fingerprints appear in no report, refusal, stdout or stderr, against a positive control. All disposable state is confined to a temporary root removed on success and refusal.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The canary confirms the exact model is available and names a permitted auth source

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ SPLIT FROM ACC-0047. That criterion accepted both TSK-0029 and TSK-0030, and TSK-0030 depends on TSK-0029, so the merge could not be accepted until normalisation was built as well. ACC-0047 now covers the merge primitive alone; this criterion covers the decision to rewrite the entry, which TSK-0029's merge then applies. ⚠️ PROOF BEFORE REWRITE, NEVER A CONSTRUCTED TARGET. An entry whose equivalence cannot be proved is left exactly as `pi install -l` wrote it; guessing the portable form would point the project at a directory nobody showed was the pinned package.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The literal package entry that `pi install -l` wrote is rewritten to the portable `../.planning/pi-package` spelling only after both spellings are shown to canonicalise to the same package directory on the running platform, and the rewrite is applied through the settings merge so every third-party package entry and unrelated key is preserved. When equivalence cannot be established - the entry resolves somewhere else, does not resolve, or cannot be read - normalisation is refused and `.pi/settings.json` is left byte-identical.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The package entry is normalised only after canonical equivalence is proved

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138. A complete run against an environment-authenticated provider — asserted from the preflight's own line — with research enabled and its connection checked. THE FILE SET IS WHAT THIS RUN ADDED OR CHANGED: git's own answer before and after, NUL-delimited so a newline in a path cannot read as two entries, with the rename form handled. There is no exemption list: every entry in that set is read, and one that is not a regular file fails. A file the operator writes before the run, carrying a key and a path of its own, is outside the set, which is how the boundary is observable. Every file in it carries no credential, nothing derived from one (sha256 hex and base64, base64 of the key, a prefix), no authorisation header, no path belonging to this machine by value OR BY SHAPE, and not even the names of the credential variables. `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are asserted in that set by name; the ignored consent and compatibility records are asserted not to be. Deleting the assertions fails nothing, because nothing currently leaks, so what proves the scan bites is injected leaks: a credential variable's name in settings, an absolute path in a generated document, and the research key in the project record are each caught, as is widening the set back to the whole after-state.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: After a complete setup against an environment-authenticated provider and an enabled research connection, every committed file the setup produced or modified is asserted to contain no API key, token, authorisation header, credential-derived fingerprint, or absolute user path - the set taken from what the setup actually wrote, not from a list fixed in advance - and `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are each asserted explicitly by name.
acceptanceCriteria.title: A complete setup commits no secret and no absolute home path

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138. The project id is minted once and reused on later runs, and a completed run leaves no journal. A project with no coverage is shown exactly the three choices the state library returns, with the ignore block's own bytes; answering nothing, `stop`, `user-state` or anything unrecognised stops with nothing written; a non-interactive run refuses on the same object with no `.pi`, no content root and no ignore file — asserted by those paths not existing. External state is offered, which this criterion permits now that AST-0047 (on EVD-0081) establishes relocation for the pinned runtime: `--session-dir` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` reach a per-user root without committing an absolute path, and a run in that mode commits no `sessionDir` at all.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: A complete setup creates the stable non-secret project ID once and reuses an existing one rather than minting a second identity. Where coverage is missing, interactive setup renders exactly the three choices the state library returns - the exact ignore block with its bytes, external state, and stopping - and non-interactive setup refuses on the same object, with the refusal occurring before setup has written any session, consent, compatibility or journal file, asserted by those paths not existing. External state is offered only once relocation support for the pinned runtime has been established.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Setup mints the project ID, renders the coverage choices, and refuses before writing runtime data

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138. An interactive run prints the canonical project directory the decision applies to and asks about it; `--trust approve` records an approval with no prompt, and answers over a recorded decision because it is the operator answering now; a run with nobody to ask refuses WITHOUT REACHING THE QUESTION, measured as zero questions asked. Only an explicit yes approves and only an explicit no denies: a closed input, an empty line and an unreadable answer each leave the trust store with no decision. A denial is reported as not ready, nothing is registered, the journal is removed, and the scaffold that survives passes Kiln's own plan linter; Pi loads none of the package's tools for that project, which is the same fact from the runtime's side. THE BROWSER-ONLY ROUTE IS SERVED, NOT INFERRED: the application is started against that denied project and asked for a page, which returns a rendered document — content that validates does not establish that a server can read it. LIMIT: what is not exercised is `npm start`'s production path, which installs and builds before serving, because a test may not run an install.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Interactive setup displays the canonical project directory the decision applies to and obtains an approval or a denial for it. `--trust approve` records an approval without a prompt. Non-interactive setup neither prompts nor assumes: with no pre-existing decision and no explicit approval it refuses. A denial is reported as not ready - setup does not describe the agent as usable - while the planning scaffold is left intact and valid and the browser-only start remains available.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Setup obtains the trust decision for the path it names, and never defaults one

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ REOPENED 2026-09-14 (F114): THE MODEL RECEIVED NO CAPABILITY DECLARATION. EVD-0103 observed the handler result and the session's `tool_execution_end.details`, not the provider-facing tool content. `rendered()` in `pi-package/extensions/kiln.js` returned `{output, details}` with no `content`, and Pi sends a tool result without `content` to the provider as `(no tool output)`. A real `/kiln-start` session measured it on 2026-09-14: `kiln_project_status` executed without error and the provider received exactly that placeholder. The historical evidence and its link are kept unchanged. This criterion returns to pass only on supplemental evidence that the provider-facing tool message carries the rendered result. ⚠️ RESTORED TO PASS 2026-09-14 ON EVD-0106: commit 81f69a9 returns every result as text content equal to its rendering, and CI run 34812083727 observed it at the handler boundary for all 28 tools and in a real provider request for kiln_capability. ⚠️ TSK-0045's STATEMENT ALREADY PROMISED THIS AND NOTHING ACCEPTED IT. That task registers the research and validation adapters, delegation, AND the Kiln capability signature, but its only criterion was ACC-0065, which is about the write discipline of mutation wrappers. The capability tool could have been registered wrongly, or not at all, without a single criterion noticing. ⚠️ THE PACKAGE DECLARES, THE TOOL RETURNS, A CONSUMER COMPARES. ACC-0063 covers the declaration agreeing with the manifest; this covers the tool handing that declaration back intact; ACC-0075 covers a delegation refusing a child whose signature is absent or drifted. Three criteria, three owners, one chain - and no single one of them is the whole claim.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The registered Kiln capability tool, called in a session that loaded the package, returns the package's own versioned signature declaration unchanged: the same version and the same resource names the package declares, with nothing added, dropped or rewritten in transit. A session that did not load the package has no such tool to call, and that difference is what a consumer comparing an expected signature against a returned one relies on.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The capability tool returns exactly the package's declared signature

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ REOPENED 2026-09-14 (F114): NO RESEARCH OR VALIDATION RESULT OR REFUSAL REACHED THE MODEL. EVD-0103 observed the adapters' handler results and refusals, not the provider-facing tool content. `rendered()` in `pi-package/extensions/kiln.js` returned `{output, details}` with no `content`, and Pi sends a tool result without `content` to the provider as `(no tool output)`. A real `/kiln-start` session measured it on 2026-09-14: `kiln_project_status` executed without error and the provider received exactly that placeholder. The historical evidence and its link are kept unchanged. This criterion returns to pass only on supplemental evidence that the provider-facing tool message carries the rendered result. ⚠️ RESTORED TO PASS 2026-09-14 ON EVD-0106: commit 81f69a9 returns every result as text content equal to its rendering, and CI run 34812083727 observed it at the handler boundary for all 28 tools and in a real provider request for kiln_capability. ⚠️ SPLIT FROM ACC-0065, WHICH ACCEPTED TWO TASKS THAT DO NOT DEPEND ON EACH OTHER. That criterion is about the write discipline of mutation wrappers - TSK-0044's work - and would have held TSK-0045 behind it while describing almost none of what TSK-0045 builds. ⚠️ A CAPABILITY CALL IS A READ, AND "CHANGES NOTHING" MEANS NO PERSISTED CHANGE. It mutates no planning content, no configuration and no stored state - no credential cached, no choice recorded, no file written. It does NOT mean the call touches nothing: `research_capability` makes a live request to the backend and `validation_capability` runs the interpreter, because #121 requires a capability to be PROVEN rather than declared, and #67 measured what a declared-but-unusable capability costs. A test asserting no request and no subprocess would contradict the rule the probes exist to satisfy; what must be asserted is that nothing persisted changed. ⚠️ DELEGATION IS NO LONGER HERE (F80, 2026-09-12). This criterion required each registered delegation tool to call "the existing implementation in `lib/`", and no delegation runtime exists there: it is CMP-0036's, built by TSK-0053 and TSK-0054, which TSK-0045 does not depend on. As written the criterion could not be satisfied by the task it accepts. `kiln_delegate` is now registered by TSK-0053 beside the runtime it builds, under its own criterion. ⚠️ THE FIVE WIRE NAMES ARE UNPREFIXED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE (F79). `research_capability`, `research_search`, `research_fetch`, `validation_capability` and `validation_run` are the names `lib/specialists/contract.mjs` requires by key and `verifyChild` checks a child against; renaming them to `kiln_*` would break the contract and the child-signature check. ⚠️ THE SIGNATURE TOOL IS ACC-0109's, NOT THIS ONE'S. `kiln_capability` returning the package's declaration unchanged is accepted there; this covers the adapters beside it. ⚠️ THE PI WRAPPER IS THE DISCLOSURE BOUNDARY; THE VALIDATION CONTROLLER IS DELIBERATELY NOT (F84, 2026-09-12). Measured against the real lib/validation/: a validation_run result carries absolute machine paths by four routes - failure.message when provisioning fails (the interpreter and the vpw-tier1- workspace), destroy.retainedPath and the retained-workspace omission reason when cleanup leaves the workspace behind, and executions[].stderr or stdout when a job prints its own paths, as a Python traceback does. The controller keeps those precise paths on purpose, as diagnostics for its own callers, and is not changed. The Pi wrapper renders a sanitised COPY - the exact workspace root becomes <workspace> with its relative tail kept, the interpreter, temporary directory and home become <path>, and a general absolute-path scrub runs last - and leaves the controller object untouched. A separate controller issue is warranted only if another model-facing or persisted consumer shows a controller result without going through this boundary. ⚠️ CREDENTIAL BOUNDARY (D5). Import and registration read no environment. At handler invocation, the wrapper delegates without collecting credentials for redaction; the invoked research and validation implementations may read their own permitted environment inputs. The validation controller constructs the allowlisted child environment, and tests prove a planted credential reaches neither the controller result nor the rendered result.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each registered research and validation tool performs its work by calling the existing implementation in `lib/` rather than restating its rules: no capability decision, retrieval policy or validation rule is re-implemented in the wrapper. A capability call reports what is available and changes nothing - no planning content, no configuration and no stored state. Every result and every refusal is structured data, and neither carries a credential, a credential-derived value or an absolute user path.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The research, validation and delegation adapters call the implementations that already exist

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ REGISTRATION MOVED HERE FROM TSK-0045 (F80, 2026-09-12). TSK-0045 promised to register a delegation adapter over an implementation that does not exist: the delegation runtime is CMP-0036's, TSK-0045 depends only on TSK-0043, and its criterion required each adapter to call "the existing implementation in `lib/`". The registration now sits with the runtime it wraps. ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER. Whether the runtime's own rules hold is ACC-0076's; whether a child without the Kiln capability signature is refused is ACC-0075's. This covers only the boundary between Pi and that runtime - which is why it evaluates CMP-0032 rather than CMP-0036.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: The registered `kiln_delegate` tool performs a delegation by calling the delegation runtime it is registered beside, and restates none of that runtime's rules: not the child's launch arguments, not the task binding, not model or thinking-level inheritance, not the intersected tool allowlist, not the timeout, not the abort propagated to the process tree, and not the cleanup of temporary material. The wrapper adds only the Pi-facing schema and the rendering of a result. Every result and every refusal is structured data returned to the caller rather than thrown as prose, and neither carries a credential, a credential-derived value or an absolute user path.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The delegation tool adds a schema and a rendering, and no rule of its own

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ DEFERRED FROM TSK-0046 ON PURPOSE (O1 and F88, 2026-09-13). TSK-0046 promised these seven, and no canonical definition carries any of them: `stages/*.json` has a name, a decision owner, outputs and exit criteria, and nothing else. A generator asked to emit them would have to write them into its own templates or borrow another field, which recreates exactly the drift CMP-0033 exists to prevent - two descriptions of one pipeline, each invisible from the other. So the definitions gain the fields first, and generation follows. ⚠️ PURPOSE WAS NEARLY BORROWED (F88). The first generator printed `producesProse` under Purpose. That field describes outputs; relabelling it is inference by another route, and it is refused for the same reason a template default is. ⚠️ A TEMPLATE DEFAULT IS A FAILURE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. A skill that says 'delegate as appropriate' because its definition was silent reads exactly like one whose definition said so; refusing the definition is the only way the gap stays visible. ⚠️ THE SPLIT, STATED EXACTLY (corrected 2026-09-20, D50-D56). The earlier wording said delegations and the mutation boundary both "name roles, not rules", which is true of one and misleading about the other. Three separate authorities apply. (1) DELEGATION ROLES AND CAPABILITIES ARE CHECKED AGAINST THE SPECIALIST CONTRACTS. A delegation declares `role` and `capabilities` independently; the loader validates the role against `ROLES` and requires the declared capabilities to equal `contractFor(role).requiredCapabilities`, sorted and unique. It never derives or replaces them, so a definition and a contract that disagree are a refusal rather than a silent rewrite. A role whose contract requires nothing declares `"capabilities": []` explicitly, and a stage that delegates nowhere declares `"delegations": []`. (2) CREATION AUTHORITY REMAINS `produces`, AND THE MUTATION BOUNDARY DOES NOT RESTATE IT. `stages/` already defines what a stage produces and `lib/stages.mjs` opens by warning that two hand-maintained descriptions of one pipeline disagree. A `mayCreate` list would be that second description, so there is none. (3) `mutationBoundary` NAMES CANONICAL NON-CREATION OPERATIONS. Its `mayMutate` entries are operation identifiers - the registry mutation keys plus `writeStageDocument`, `writeStageAttestation` and `setTypeActivation` - not artifact types and not tool wire names. It therefore says what a stage may CHANGE, while `produces` says what it may CREATE, and neither can be read as a weaker copy of the other. This still depends on TSK-0051, because the roster and the contracts it settled are what (1) is checked against.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each canonical stage definition in `stages/*.json` declares its purpose, its method, its rules for selecting the next question or activity, its allowed delegations with the capabilities each requires, its mutation boundary, its approval boundary and its expected completion summary, and each generated `kiln-stage-<stage-id>` skill carries those seven from its definition. None of them is supplied by the generator's templates or inferred from another field - in particular a stage's purpose is not taken from `producesProse`, which describes its outputs. The generator refuses a definition that lacks a required field rather than filling it in, and the check fails, naming the skill, when any generated field no longer matches its definition.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every stage skill carries its purpose, method, next activity, delegations and boundaries from the canonical definition

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Created 2026-09-13 (D15) from the persistence clause ACC-0068 used to carry. It belongs to TSK-0049's continuous intake capture rather than to TSK-0048's first turn. No typed stage-document writer exists today: `lib/tools/` writes typed artifacts under `data/` only, and nothing writes `stages/*.md`. TSK-0049 has to add one. ACC-0069's adaptive second question is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: When the operator answers during a stage, the answer is written into that stage's document - for Stage 1, the intake document - through a registered typed stage-document writer, never by editing the file directly. What is written keeps the operator's own wording verbatim and separate from the orchestrator's interpretation of it, and the writer refuses a write outside the content root's stage documents.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The operator's answer is persisted through a typed stage-document writer, wording kept apart from interpretation

acceptanceCriteria.notes: Created 2026-09-13 (F98, D14). ACC-0068 now accepts only what Kiln deterministically supplies to the session. What a real model then does with it is behaviour, and a scripted provider cannot establish it: the script chooses the reply before any model is asked. So the user-visible first turn is observed here, in the clean-consumer journey, with a real model and a retained record a human judges.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: In the clean-consumer journey, on a fresh project started with `/kiln-start` against a real configured model, the orchestrator's first user-visible Stage 1 turn asks exactly one question, proposes no architecture, requirement set or solution, and calls no mutating tool. The turn is retained as recorded output, and its judgement - one question, no solution - is made by a human reviewer against that record, not by the model and not by a scripted provider.
acceptanceCriteria.title: In the clean-consumer journey, the first Stage 1 turn asks one question and proposes no solution

acceptanceCriteria.notes:
Created 2026-09-18 under TSK-0050. The task's statement carries two obligations and ACC-0070 tested only one: show-before-doing had no criterion, so delivering it would have been work no criterion accepted. This is a single orchestrator-wide behaviour stated once, not TSK-0071's per-stage mutation policy: TSK-0071 owns a per-stage mutation-boundary field, and this criterion declares no stage-definition field. Like ACC-0069 it is a model-behaviour claim, so its evidence needs a retained real-model record judged by a person. The deterministic suite can show that the instruction is delivered, not that it is followed.

Delivery is the every-turn stage-context frame, as a global preamble ahead of the stage-skill block and outside it. Neither the `/kiln-start` prompt nor the packaged planning skill governs every later turn: the prompt is read once on the fresh turn, and the stage skill is per-stage content a consumer may override. The frame is rebuilt on every `before_agent_start`, so the preamble is the only delivery point that holds for the whole session.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Before calling a tool that creates or mutates a typed artifact, the orchestrator states in a separate turn which artifact it proposes to create or change and what the change would be, and waits for the operator. If the operator rejects the proposal, cancels, or does not reply, no mutating tool call is made. Capturing an operator's own answer into a stage document is excluded, because that records the operator's reply rather than proposing a change to the project. Approval, activation and attestation are governed by ACC-0070 rather than by this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The orchestrator states a material change before making it

acceptanceCriteria.notes: PASS 2026-09-24 on EVD-0142, accepted on review. acceptanceCriteria.notes: Evidence recorded 2026-09-24 in EVD-0147, and left not-evaluated for review. The control passed in all four cells of CI run 36077139114. In the earlier red run 36076748293 it failed once on Windows Node 22, at its launch step, from F130 mechanism 2, after its compat assertions had passed. ⚠️ STATEMENT AMENDED 2026-09-25 on review. Control (2) had said the child's file contains no `apiKey`, but the canary intentionally writes the provider's `apiKey` as `$NAME`; that exception is now stated and tested on the file's bytes. Refusing credential-NAMED keys could not show that a value under an innocuous key is non-secret, so the accepted values are now a closed contract, and any string outside it is refused. Stays not-evaluated for review. ⚠️ PASS 2026-09-25 on EVD-0147, on review. acceptanceCriteria.statement: For a custom provider whose `models.json` declares `compat`, the live canary's child receives the `compat` configuration Pi resolves for the selected model. Measured against a local loopback provider: the request observed at the provider matches the request that configuration produces, and the compatibility record written from that run matches the same configuration. Controls: (1) changing `compat` after a passed canary makes the stored record fail to prove the next launch; (2) the configuration passed to the child is closed, and anything outside it is refused before any child is created. It has no `apiKey`, `headers` or `authHeader` at the provider or model level, and no key named for a credential at any depth. A string value may appear only in the provider's `baseUrl` (with no user, password, query or fragment) and `api`; in each model's `id`, `name` and `input` modalities; in compat fields whose values Pi restricts to fixed literals, and only as one of those literals; and as a chat-template variable's `$var`. Elsewhere, including `samplingParams`, chat-template arguments and structured routing fields, values are numbers, booleans or null. A model whose request needs any other value cannot be proved by the live check. (3) The child's `models.json` is checked byte for byte. Its only credential field is the provider's `apiKey`, which the canary writes as exactly `$NAME` of the declared variable, and it contains no credential value, no header and no other credential field.
acceptanceCriteria.title: The live canary sends a custom provider's resolved compat configuration and nothing credential-bearing

acceptanceCriteria.notes: ✅ PASS 2026-09-26 on EVD-0154: every refusal reason at every research entry point before the key is read or a request made, both state modes, the record destination check, and the key withheld from both children; CI run 36244920683, four cells.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each research entry point - the research_capability, research_search and research_fetch tools Kiln registers in Pi, research:search and research:record (bin/research.mjs), and research:probe (bin/research-probe.mjs) - refuses unless the project's committed research choice is tavily AND this computer holds a standing research grant for it, read from where the run keeps its runtime state: project-local, or the per-user root setup keeps with --local-state user. The refusal happens before TAVILY_API_KEY is read and before any request is made, and it names a stable reason: no project context, the project record unreadable, research not chosen, this computer's consent record unreadable, no standing grant, or a local-state mode that is neither project nor user. An unreadable record of either kind refuses; it is never read as permission. The context is explicit: Pi receives the project root and state mode from the supervisor, and the commands require --project-root and take --local-state; nothing is guessed from the working directory. research:record additionally refuses, before fetching, when its evidence destination (the content-root rule or PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR) belongs to a project other than the one whose consent was read. When research is not permitted at launch, TAVILY_API_KEY is kept out of the environment of both of the supervisor's children. Each refusal reason is shown at each entry point by a test that also shows no key was read and no request was made, and the permitted cases, project-local and per-user, are shown to reach the key only after the gate.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Research is refused at every entry point unless the project chose Tavily and this computer granted it

All three belong to FILE-ROUTED MDX, which DEC-0020 explicitly rejected: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build so an edit changes nothing, which fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ HOW IT GOT IN IS WORTH RECORDING. Those settings came from the PROBE that measured the rejected option. Moving them to `app/` produced `Route (app)` with `○ /`, and the skeleton is left alone as a colocated non-route file — `server.mjs` is not a `page`, `layout` or `route`, and `.mjs` is not in the default `pageExtensions`. ⚠️ A build that SUCCEEDS while rendering nothing you wrote is the failure mode worth remembering here: `✓ Compiled successfully` was printed both times, and only the route table said which files Next.js had actually found. ⚠️ VERIFIED FROM CLEAN: `.next` removed, `npm run shell:build` from scratch, `next start` bound to 127.0.0.1 only (confirmed against the listening socket, not assumed from the flag), HTTP 200 with the expected body, process terminated and the port confirmed free. `npm audit` reports zero vulnerabilities after adding next, react and react-dom. ⚠️ NOT DONE HERE, on purpose: no MDX integration of any kind, no watcher, no launcher that owns processes, and no planning-content read. The route reads nothing — a convenience read would be the first violation of REQ-0021's confinement, whose own enforcement (TSK-0006, TSK-0015) does not exist yet.

It arrives with the review action, where it can be examined on its own. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27. Five static tests, each falsified: removing a `connection()`, importing `node:fs`, importing `lib/` directly, and adding a synchronous export each turn the suite red. ⚠️ THE ADAPTER GAINED ONE NAME, deliberately and reviewably: `readStageDocs`, taken from the PUBLISHER rather than written fresh. It already owns what a stage document is — `.md` and `.mdx`, dotfiles ignored, anything else REFUSED — and a second reader in the application would have quietly disagreed with the package about which files count. ⚠️ A PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH (AST-0037): the reader was designed expecting bundling to break `toolRoot()`, and it did not. It could be built last, after there is more to check — and then it would arrive to find a codebase already full of violations, and the pressure would be to weaken the rule rather than fix the code. Built here, it constrains every task after it while the cost of complying is one file at a time. ⚠️ The failing fixtures are not optional polish (ACC-0024): a check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. ⚠️ SPLIT 2026-08-27. This half needs only the adapter to exist, so it moves earlier and no longer waits on the reader. The read and `<Suspense>` confinement analysis is its sibling. ⚠️ ACC-0024 is satisfied by the PAIR, not by this task alone: both halves must be shown to fail on their own fixtures before the criterion passes. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Three fixtures, eight tests, one lint command, and three defects found before the check was trusted — two by the fixtures (an off-by-one line, and a lazy pattern spanning two statements) and one by running it (a reachability-scoped check that examined almost nothing). ⚠️ A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND IN AN EARLIER TASK'S TEST. It now uses this task's comment-stripping scanner: a check that cannot tell an import from prose is a check that punishes documentation. ⚠️ Fixture adapters deliberately omit `import "server-only"`. Everything under `test/` is collected by `node --test`, and the marker throws outside the RSC compiler (AST-0033), so a fixture carrying it crashed the suite for a reason unrelated to what it tests.

Ship fixtures containing both shapes and prove the check fails on each.

⚠️ Request-time compilation, never file-routed `app/**/page.mdx`: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build, which satisfies REQ-0017 and silently fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ The compiler and plugin chain are PINNED. Changing the MDX version or adding any remark, rehype or recma plugin reopens security validation before it ships. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Twelve tests against a real `@mdx-js/mdx` compile, each rejection asserting a path AND a line:column, plus a control proving an unguarded compile really does evaluate the expression — without which a rejection and a silent strip would be indistinguishable. Falsified three ways: removing the ESM rule, disabling the unmapped-component check, and replacing rejection with stripping each turn the suite red. ⚠️ THE FORMAT DEFAULT WAS THE FINDING (AST-0038), and it was caught by the production probe rather than by the tests — the mapped component rendered as a bare `

The test fixture is now deliberately named `.md`, so dropping `format: "mdx"` fails nineteen tests. ⚠️ `components.js` is written with `createElement` rather than JSX so that plain Node can import it. A JSX version would have forced the tests to build their own component map, which would have made them a check on a stub rather than on the vocabulary that ships.

Surface the failure to the operator. Stripping may sit beneath the rejection as defence in depth and may never be the observable behaviour.
accepted.title: Build the restricted MDX compiler with rejection diagnostics

accepted.notes: ⚠️ A comment-line keepalive is ignored by the client parser (AST-0036) — it keeps the socket warm and leaves the page looking healthy. The heartbeat must be an event a listener can fire on. ⚠️ No event buffer, event id or `Last-Event-ID`: events are hints and never deltas, so a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up. ⚠️ Logging a watcher failure to the server console is explicitly not enough. THE TASK-BINDING OBSERVER (D42). `taskBindingObserved` is produced by a private Kiln observer extension loaded explicitly into the child. Its `before_provider_request` hook inspects the FINAL provider payload for a framed task carrying a one-time nonce, a length and a digest, and emits only a minimal attestation - never the payload - over a dedicated extra pipe the parent opens. The parent validates that attestation against the nonce, length and digest it generated. A mismatch in any of the three produces no binding.

REJECTED SOURCES, AND WHY. Model output and ordinary JSON events are not acceptable: both are things the child says about itself, which is the failure REQ-0026 exists to prevent. Writing or hashing the prompt file is not acceptable either: it proves the parent PREPARED the task, not that the child CONSUMED it. The provider payload at the last moment before dispatch is the first point where consumption is observable, and the hook runs inside the child but reports on the child's outbound request rather than on its own account of itself.

WHAT THE ATTESTATION MAY CARRY. The nonce, the length and the digest, and nothing else. Never the task text, never a credential or a credential-derived value, never an absolute path. The payload is neither retained nor returned.

THE TSK-0054 BOUNDARY (D43). This task builds the runtime and registers `kiln_delegate`, and it must pass every run through the EXISTING `verifyChild` gate before any substantive output is exposed. There is no temporarily permissive delegation path. Expanding and proving the complete refusal matrix - malformed events, nonzero exit, provider mismatch, out-of-role writes - is TSK-0054's, under ACC-0075. In short: this task produces the run record and gates on it; TSK-0054 judges the full set of ways a record can be bad.

PROCESS TEARDOWN (D44). The runtime reuses `trackDescendants` and `stopTree` from `lib/supervisor.mjs` and owns one child tree wrapping those primitives. No second PID-only termination implementation, and no change to supervisor behaviour unless an unavailable seam forces a separate decision, which would be recorded before it is made.
