accepted.notes:
Scope settled 2026-09-20, before implementation. ACC-0075 needs no amendment: it already names all eight causes, and this task builds the detection for them.

THE MATRIX AUDIT FOUND THREE CAUSES WITH NO CHECK AT ALL. A nonzero exit is captured as `run.exit` and never consulted. A line that fails `JSON.parse` is silently skipped, so a child emitting garbage around one valid assistant message is accepted. And `CHILD_REFUSED.OUT_OF_ROLE_WRITE` is defined with `mayWrite` implemented and no production caller anywhere, so nothing observes a write outside a role's boundary. It also found that answer extraction runs BEFORE verification: `answerFrom(stdout)` is called inside `runChild` while the gate runs after it, so the assistant text is selected before anything is checked. The refusal path drops it today, which is why the criterion is not violated, but the ordering makes that incidental rather than structural.

D47 TWO NEW WIRE CODES, EVERY EXISTING LITERAL PRESERVED. `NONZERO_EXIT: "child-exited-nonzero"` and `EVENTS_MALFORMED: "child-events-malformed"`. "The child did not finish" and "the child's stream could not be read" are different facts from the five already coded, and a caller that cannot tell them apart cannot act on either. The pinned wire-contract test in test/specialist-contract.test.mjs is extended rather than replaced.

D48 A SELECTION MISMATCH IS NOT A MISSING CAPABILITY. `SELECTION_MISMATCH: "child-selection-mismatch"`. A child answering under a provider or model nobody asked for fails for a reason a delegating model would otherwise be told was a missing tool, and would look for the wrong fix. A missing or malformed report still resolves to `capability-missing`, because in that case the child genuinely cannot demonstrate its tools.

D49 ABSENCE STAYS PRIMARY; OBSERVATION IS A FAIL-SAFE. `--tools` and the measured active registry keep an out-of-role tool unavailable, which is the boundary #67 asks for and the one a child cannot argue with. The package extension is NOT made role-aware: that would put a second, weaker copy of the write boundary inside the child and would change a launch protocol that was just measured. Instead Pi's own `tool_execution_start` events are parsed, and an out-of-role mutation that nevertheless STARTS is a refusal. Starting is sufficient: a handler that failed may already have partially mutated state, so waiting for `tool_execution_end` would be waiting for damage to finish. The stable code remains `out-of-role-write`.

NOT READ, OPERATIONALLY. Rejected assistant prose is never selected as the answer, returned, logged or included in refusal details. Buffering process stdout is permitted and necessary: malformed-event detection requires reading the stream. `answerFrom` moves after acceptance so the ordering enforces it.

PRECEDENCE. A run can fail several ways at once, so the order the checks run in is itself a contract and gets its own test: timeout or abort, then malformed events, then nonzero exit, then the task binding, then the selection, then out-of-role writes, then capabilities and signatures. Cheapest and most fundamental first, and nothing about the child's own account is consulted before the facts the process itself supplies.

FIVE REVIEW CORRECTIONS, APPLIED BEFORE THE MUTATION GATE. F39 the binding now refuses at its own step rather than waiting for `verifyChild`, so a child that was never given the task is never refused for a wrong model or a write instead. F40 the write boundary is `mayWrite` over the canonical operation a wire name resolves to, not membership of the allowlist: `active` is the role's tools intersected with the host registry, so a host missing a tool would otherwise make a declared write look out of role, and a read the role simply was not given would be reported as an attempted mutation. F41 a `toolName` this host does not register makes the stream unreadable and is never copied anywhere; every name in an observation comes from Kiln's own table. F42 a type is not a shape: the event types the gate consumes are checked for the fields it reads, and the answer and the native selection are taken only from `message_end` and `turn_end`. The shapes are measured, not assumed - a real child run showed `message_update` carries no `message` at all, which a guessed rule refused. F43 the matrix fixture takes a LIST of faults, so every adjacent pair in the precedence order is a genuine double failure; `bindingDetail` is gone from observations because it quotes the child's own material, and `durationMs` is restored and read when each observation is built.

components.notes: ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY IS 'NEVER PATH', and it is a correctness rule rather than a preference. A globally installed Pi may exist at any version; if a specialist child resolves a different binary from the orchestrator, the capability signature the delegation verifier compares was measured against a runtime that is not the one that answered.
components.responsibility: Be the only route by which any Pi process is started. Resolve the exact pinned CLI from the tool's own node_modules, report its version, refuse a version that does not match the pin, and hand every caller — setup, the user-facing session, and every specialist child — the same executable invoked through the current Node binary with shell interpolation disabled. Discovering Pi on PATH is outside this component and outside the product.
components.title: Pinned Pi runtime

components.notes: ⚠️ IT REUSES THE EXISTING LOCK RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. The initializer already owns `<project>/.planning-init.lock`; a second lock beside it would let setup and initialization interleave on the same files while each believed it held the project. The initializer and the ignore owner must therefore accept an already-held transaction instead of acquiring their own. ⚠️ THERE IS NO --force. A malformed file is a refusal, because the only thing --force could mean here is overwriting something the operator wrote and setup could not parse.
components.responsibility: Own one project-wide lock for the whole of setup, and make every lasting write happen under a plan rather than in sequence: canonicalise and print each target before mutating, schema-validate every file it may read or merge, probe same-directory temporary-file creation and atomic rename in each parent it will write to, record the identity of each existing file, re-compare that identity immediately before each merge, and maintain a non-secret journal that names the last completed phase so an interruption resumes rather than restarts.
components.title: Setup transaction

components.notes: ⚠️ THIS IS A REFACTOR OF WORKING CODE, NOT A NEW CAPABILITY. `lib/initialize-project.mjs` already owns planning, append safety, recorded idempotency and the deliberately-deleted-block rule. The failure this component prevents is a second appender in setup with different idempotency rules — which is how a file people edit by hand acquires two Kiln blocks.
components.responsibility: Be the single owner of every Kiln edit to the consumer's `.gitignore`: plan the change without writing, append rather than rewrite, take the line ending from the file, record what it did, migrate an exact unmodified legacy block to the extended block under the same lock and atomic-write discipline, and never restore a block the operator deliberately removed or edited.
components.title: Project ignore owner

components.notes: ⚠️ THE FILE HAS TWO AUTHORS. `pi install -l` writes it and so does Kiln, and it is also a file the operator may hand-edit. Every one of those is a legitimate writer, so the merge is the boundary: Kiln owns four groups of keys covering six keys in all, and must be able to prove it touched nothing else. ⚠️ NO SECRET EVER LANDS HERE. This file is committed on purpose, which is exactly why an API key, an OAuth token or an absolute home path reaching it is a disclosure rather than an untidiness. ⚠️ THERE IS NO SCHEMA VERSION TO CHECK. Pi's settings format has no version field, so the earlier requirement to refuse an unknown schema version had nothing to read; what is refused is malformed JSON, a non-object root, or an invalid value in a field Kiln owns, and every unknown field is kept. ⚠️ WRITER ORDER FOR THE PACKAGE ENTRY: `pi install -l` creates the literal entry; TSK-0030 proves canonical equivalence and chooses the portable spelling; TSK-0029's merge is the only mechanism that writes that decision, preserving every other entry. ⚠️ PI'S OWN LOCK IS HONOURED. Pi saves project settings under a `proper-lockfile` lock on the file, re-reading it and writing in place, and Kiln's transaction lock does not block it - so a Pi save landing between Kiln's final identity check and its rename would be lost. The merge takes the same `proper-lockfile` lock, as a direct pinned dependency, across that final check and the atomic write, without importing Pi's unexported storage class. ⚠️ TRAILING NEWLINE FOLLOWS THE FILE. Pi writes none; a merge that added one would change bytes on every alternation with a Pi save. An existing file keeps its style and a new file has none. ⚠️ KEY ORDER IS THE ORDER PI'S OWN SAVE PRODUCES. Pi parses and re-serializes this file with JavaScript's JSON, which places integer-like property names such as `"1"` ahead of every other key in ascending numeric order. Kiln's merge does the same, so ordinary string keys keep their relative order and integer-like names land where the next Pi save would put them anyway. A token-preserving JSON editor could promise their original textual position, but Pi's next save would discard it, so that is not the boundary. ⚠️ THE SKILL OVERRIDE IS OBSERVED, NOT ASSUMED: EVD-0081 recorded a consumer override directory registered through the settings `skills` array loading instead of the packaged skill, and the packaged skill loading when it was removed.
components.responsibility: Merge only Kiln's owned fields into the project's `.pi/settings.json` - the local package entry, the skill-override path `../planning-content/skills-overrides`, the selected default provider, model and thinking level, and `sessionDir: ".pi/sessions"` when project-local state is selected (removing Kiln's owned `sessionDir` when it is not, so no external path is committed) - preserving the value of every unrelated key, package entry and unknown Pi or third-party field and the relative order of ordinary string keys, with integer-like property names following Pi's and JavaScript's JSON serialization order, refusing malformed JSON, a non-object root or an invalid value in a Kiln-owned field rather than replacing the file, preserving the file's trailing-newline style, and changing no bytes when the desired state is already present.
components.title: Pi settings merge

components.notes: ⚠️ THE EXTERNAL MODE IS NO LONGER CONDITIONAL — three relocation routes were proved on both platforms (AST-0047), so `--session-dir` supplied at launch reaches an external root without committing an absolute path. ⚠️ THE FIVE PERSISTED SHAPES ARE NOW SPECIFIED AND VALIDATED (DEC-0033), which is what stage 5's data-model criterion was waiting on: each has a schema, a per-record version, a declared location, a committed/ignored classification, and refusals for the credential material and absolute home paths REQ-0024 forbids. What is specified is the SHAPE; the code that writes them is still the setup transaction's work.
components.responsibility: Decide and enforce where session transcripts, consent records, compatibility results and setup journals live: by default under the outer project's ignored `.pi/sessions/` and `.pi/runtime/`, or, when explicitly selected, under an external per-user root derived from the committed non-secret project ID. Refuse to write any runtime data before the chosen location's protection is in place, and never commit an absolute user path in order to reach it.
components.title: Local-state policy

components.notes: ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS SETTLED AND MEASURED. Decision #67(a) chose writing Pi's user trust file directly; the PM withdrew that on 2026-09-02 in favour of a supported route, and QST-0026 then found one: `ProjectTrustStore`, exported from the package root of pi 0.84.4, records a decision keyed by canonical directory that a later non-interactive child honours - a grant loads the project package without `--approve`, an explicit denial prevents loading, and revocation reverts. Measured on Windows (EVD-0077) and Linux (EVD-0078) with the full control set, and stated as AST-0041. DEC-0027 is satisfiable exactly as written and `--trust approve` can ship. ⚠️ KILN DEPENDS ON THE CLASS, NEVER ON THE FILE. The store still writes `~/.pi/agent/trust.json` underneath; that shape is not Kiln's to know, and the difference between depending on a typed exported class and depending on an undocumented file is the whole of what DEC-0027 changed. ⚠️ ONLY TWO TRUST NAMES ARE ROOT EXPORTS - `ProjectTrustStore` and `hasTrustRequiringProjectResources`. `getProjectTrustOptions` and `getProjectTrustParentPath` exist in the package's internal declarations and are not reachable without importing an unexported path, which this component does not do. ⚠️ WHY THE GATE IS NOT COSMETIC: AST-0042 measured an unapproved non-interactive child loading none of the project package's tools while reporting no error, no warning and no non-zero exit. Every role boundary in Kiln is enforced by those tools, so an ungated launch produces an unconstrained model whose output looks exactly like a specialist's.
components.responsibility: Obtain, verify and report the operator's trust decision for this project's Pi resources through Pi's own supported mechanism, display the canonical project path the decision applies to, treat a denial as a first-class outcome that stops agent launch without touching the planning scaffold, and refuse a non-interactive run that has no pre-existing decision rather than defaulting one.
components.title: Project trust integration

components.notes: ⚠️ THE PROMPT'S WORDING IS PART OF THE COMPONENT. 'Check this computer for existing AI-provider and web-research connections' is what is happening; 'search for credentials' describes the same act in a way that is both more alarming and less accurate, since nothing is displayed or copied. ⚠️ A DECLINED INSPECTION PERFORMS NO READS AT ALL — not a presence check, not a registry load — and leaves setup honestly partial rather than reporting that nothing is configured.
components.responsibility: Ask before looking, and record what was granted. Obtain explicit permission before reading Pi's user authentication store, its custom-model registry, or the presence of any credential environment variable; then report sanitised availability only — provider display names, model identifiers, and present-or-absent for the research credential — contacting no external service. Persist the operator's grant where a clone does not carry it to another machine, and reopen the prompt when the provider or research choice changes.
components.title: Connection inspection and consent

components.notes: ⚠️ 'NEVER A MUTABLE ALIAS' IS A REPRODUCIBILITY RULE. A project that records `latest` records nothing: the content it produces cannot be attributed to a model, and a change of behaviour has no change of configuration to explain it.
components.responsibility: Turn discovery into a recorded decision and hold it: present available providers and exact model identifiers, require confirmation even when exactly one is available, persist the exact non-alias identifiers as project configuration, state plainly that subsequent work on this model may be billed, and at every later launch resolve that recorded selection and refuse the run if it is unavailable rather than falling back.
components.title: Model binding

components.notes: ⚠️ CUSTOM PROVIDERS MAY CONTRIBUTE NAMES ONLY DECLARATIVELY. Guessing a variable name from a provider id, or discovering one by enumerating the operator's environment for things that look like keys, is the failure this component exists to prevent — and both are the obvious implementation. ⚠️ PREFER PI'S AUTH STORE WHEN IT IS AVAILABLE, because then a child needs the variables that locate configuration rather than a copy of the credential itself. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-02 AFTER MEASUREMENT (AST-0045): this component controls what it ADDS, not everything the child ends up seeing. Windows injects HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, LOGONSERVER, SYSTEMDRIVE, TEMP, USERDOMAIN, USERNAME, USERPROFILE and WINDIR into every child whatever environment it is handed, so the boundary is a lower bound there and the original wording — that the child's environment IS the union — was not achievable. The guarantee that survives, and the one worth having, is that no credential and no unrelated secret is among what Kiln adds. ⚠️ A SECOND CONSEQUENCE: because USERPROFILE is always present on Windows, a child always resolves the default agent directory, so redirecting one requires setting PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR positively and can never be done by omitting a variable.
components.responsibility: Be the single audited statement of which environment-variable NAMES each supported provider needs on the model plane, holding no values; separate those from tool-plane names that belong to one role; construct each child's environment from the measured base runtime variables, the selected provider's model-plane names and that role's tool-plane names, adding nothing else; and classify a provider with no safe known mapping as unsupported rather than granting it a wider inheritance.
components.title: Provider credential contracts

components.notes: ⚠️ THE APPROVAL NAMES THE COST. The provider may bill for this request, so the prompt says so and names the exact model; declining leaves a valid content and browser setup and an agent that is not described as ready. ⚠️ MODEL PROSE CLAIMING TOOL SUPPORT IS NOT EVIDENCE — the observation is the tool call arriving with the right challenge, taken upstream of anything the model says about itself. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-22 (Q6): the package capability signature was replaced as a record determinant by preflightContractDigest, per DEC-0033 and proposal section 3.12, and kept as a zero-cost launch check.
components.responsibility: Prove, with one separately authorised request, that the selected provider and model actually answer and actually emit the shape of tool call Kiln depends on: expose a single read-only setup-only tool, require the model to call it with a random challenge against the declared schema, send no planning content, permit no mutation, cap the token budget, and record success only against the exact provider, model, thinking level, runtime version, preflight contract digest and non-secret endpoint identity that produced it. The package capability signature is not part of the record's key; it remains a zero-cost check at every launch.
components.title: Live model and tool canary

components.notes: ⚠️ THE COMMITTED PACKAGE ENTRY MUST BE PORTABLE. `pi install -l` writes whatever it writes; the entry that ends up in a committed settings file has to be a separator-normalised relative literal that resolves to the same directory on another operator's machine, and it may be normalised only after canonical equivalence to what Pi wrote is proved. An absolute path here breaks every clone. ⚠️ THIS COMPONENT PUBLISHES A DECLARATION; IT DOES NOT IMPLEMENT ITS CONSUMERS. The responsibility says any consumer CAN compare what loaded against what it expected, and that is a property of the declaration being machine-readable and versioned - not a promise that this component builds those comparisons. Each one is owned and accepted elsewhere: the capability tool returning the declaration unchanged is TSK-0045's, on CMP-0032; a delegation refusing a child whose signature is missing or drifted is ACC-0075's, on CMP-0036; the canary's record invalidating when what it measured changes is ACC-0062's, on CMP-0030; and refusing to launch at all over a project whose trust is not approved is ACC-0051's, on CMP-0026, which is already accepted. ⚠️ THE PACKAGE DIRECTORY IS WHERE THE COMMITTED ENTRY POINTS. TSK-0030 writes `../.planning/pi-package` into the project's settings, relative to `.pi/`; in a consumer install the tool is at `<project>/.planning/`, so that entry resolves to this component's own directory at the tool root. Until it exists, the entry that is committed points at nothing.
components.responsibility: Be the installable unit Pi loads for this project: a declared package manifest naming its extensions, skills and prompts; a registration entry point; and a machine-readable capability signature that any consumer — the supervisor, the canary, a delegation verifier — can compare against what it expected to be loaded.
components.title: Kiln Pi package

components.notes: ⚠️ DISABLING THE BUILT-INS IS THE POINT, NOT AN OPTIMISATION. Pi's default active set includes bash, write and edit — measured, not assumed. An orchestrator holding those can write planning content around the locked, validated, atomic path that decision #88 makes the only legal one, and it will, because editing a file is easier than calling a typed tool. ⚠️ THE WIRE NAMES ARE FIXED HERE, BECAUSE A TOOL NAME IS A CONTRACT. A model is told them, a specialist allowlist names them, and the package's signature declares them - three places that must agree, so they are not improvised per wrapper. ⚠️ WHO OWNS WHICH NAMES. TSK-0044 registers exactly these 22, all `kiln_`-prefixed: kiln_create_requirement, kiln_create_assertion, kiln_create_evidence, kiln_create_runbook_step, kiln_create_question, kiln_create_decision, kiln_create_component, kiln_create_acceptance_criterion, kiln_create_task, kiln_link_evidence, kiln_unlink_evidence, kiln_revise_artifact, kiln_set_lifecycle, kiln_resolve_question, kiln_link_trace, kiln_unlink_trace, kiln_set_review_status, kiln_set_type_activation, kiln_project_status, kiln_lint, kiln_read_stage_attestations, kiln_write_stage_attestation. TSK-0045 registers six more: research_capability, research_search, research_fetch, validation_capability, validation_run and kiln_capability. TSK-0053 registers kiln_delegate beside the delegation runtime it builds. kiln_preflight remains TSK-0041's and is setup-only, removed from the effective set before the user-facing session starts, so it must never appear in the orchestrator's measured registry. ⚠️ THE FIVE SPECIALIST NAMES ARE UNPREFIXED ON PURPOSE (F79, 2026-09-12). `lib/specialists/contract.mjs` requires research_capability, research_search, research_fetch, validation_capability and validation_run BY KEY, reads their measured signatures from those keys, and `verifyChild` checks a child's registry against them. A `kiln_` prefix would break the contract and the signature check to satisfy a naming habit nobody wrote down. ⚠️ AND THE `/^kiln_/` ASSERTIONS DESCRIBE TSK-0044's 22, NOT THE PACKAGE. `test/supervisor.test.mjs` and `test/pi-session-tools.test.mjs` assert that every declared and every measured tool name starts with `kiln_`. That was true of the set that existed when they were written and is not a package-wide rule; when TSK-0045 adds its names those assertions must become EXACT-SET comparisons against the declaration rather than prefix matches, which is the stronger check in any case. ⚠️ THE ORDER THE WORK GOES IN, AND WHY. First the signature declares the names, then a check compares that declaration against what registration actually produces - by calling the registration function with a recording stub, the way the package's own test already proves it registers nothing. Without that check the declared `tools` list is the one part of the signature nothing verifies, because tools are not files on disk. Then the read wrappers, then the mutation and attestation wrappers, then the launch flags that disable Pi's built-ins, and last the real-session measurement ACC-0064 asks for - which needs a session against a loopback provider, since no CLI flag lists the active tools and exits.
components.responsibility: Expose the existing typed libraries to the agent as validated Pi tools and nothing more: project status and lint reads, artifact creation and mutation through the existing registries, project-type activation, stage attestation reads and writes, the research and validation capability adapters, and delegation. Own the tool schemas and result rendering; leave every business rule in `lib/`. Launch the session with Pi's built-in filesystem and shell mutation tools disabled.
components.title: Pi tool registration

components.notes: ⚠️ THE GENERATOR EXISTS TO PREVENT ONE SPECIFIC DRIFT: the agent working confidently to exit criteria the application is not checking. Two hand-maintained descriptions of one pipeline disagree, and the disagreement is invisible from either side. ⚠️ THE NAMING RULE IS A CONTRACT (2026-09-13). Every generated skill is `kiln-stage-<stage-id>`, at `pi-package/skills/kiln-stage-<stage-id>/SKILL.md`, with that name in its frontmatter - for example `kiln-stage-01-intake` and `kiln-stage-09-handoff`. The prefix keeps them from colliding with a consumer's own skills, and the full name is the identity a consumer override must match, so it does not change without a migration. ⚠️ GENERATED AND HANDWRITTEN ARE KEPT APART. The generator owns exactly the `kiln-stage-*` skills and nothing else under `pi-package/skills/`. `kiln-planning` is handwritten, and generation and the check must never adopt it, rewrite it, report it as orphaned, or delete it; a skill directory the generator did not produce is not the generator's to judge. ⚠️ PURPOSE IS PART OF THIS COMPONENT, AND IT IS DEFERRED (F88, 2026-09-13). The responsibility above includes a stage's purpose, and the completed component will generate it. TSK-0046 does not, because no canonical purpose field exists today: `producesProse` describes what a stage produces, and printing it as a purpose would be inference rather than generation. TSK-0071 authors a purpose field in every definition and generates it from there; until then each generated skill states plainly that its purpose is not declared. ⚠️ OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE IS PI'S RESOLUTION ORDER, NOT REGISTRATION ORDER (F91, 2026-09-13). The override does not win by being registered after the packaged set; Pi 0.84.4 ranks a project-settings skill path ahead of a package resource and keeps the first skill with each name. The promise is that the consumer override wins over the packaged skill, not over every project skill path: an earlier project-settings entry holding the same identity outranks Kiln's appended override entry (R8).
components.responsibility: Generate one packaged skill per canonical stage definition, named `kiln-stage-<stage-id>`, so that stage purpose, decision owner, outputs and exit criteria are never hand-maintained twice; fail a check that writes nothing when a packaged stage skill is stale, missing or orphaned relative to `stages/`; and let a consumer override a packaged stage skill without editing the tool clone, through the project-settings `skills` entry for the consumer's override directory: Pi resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources and the first skill with a given identity wins, so the consumer's override wins over the packaged skill of that identity.
components.title: Stage skill generation and overrides

components.notes: ⚠️ IT MAY NOT ATTEST. Approving an artifact and satisfying a user-owned exit criterion are the operator's acts; an orchestrator that can do either can walk the project through its own gates. This is the boundary the Stage 1 vertical slice has to demonstrate by being refused. ⚠️ THE ORCHESTRATOR READS THROUGH KILN, NOT THROUGH PI'S READ TOOL (F95, D10, D11, 2026-09-13). Its session holds only Kiln's tools, so project identity, the current stage's blockers and next action, and the Stage 1 starter document arrive through `kiln_project_status`, and the current stage's skill is injected at `before_agent_start` exactly as Pi loaded it, override included. ⚠️ THE CONTENT-ROOT REFUSAL LIVES IN THE ORCHESTRATOR TOO (F96, F97, D13). The launcher's refusal does not reach a Pi child that re-resolves the root from an inherited override; the orchestrator refuses the tool's own content itself, unless the launcher's strict self-host marker is present, and tells the model placeholders rather than paths.
components.responsibility: Be the single persistent planning session: resolve the canonical sibling content root and refuse to operate on the tool's own planning content, derive the current stage from definitions and attestations rather than storing a duplicate status, load the matching stage skill, ask one question at a time chosen by information value, keep the operator's wording separate from its own interpretation, mutate only through registered typed tools, show material changes before making them, and resume from files and attestations when the transcript is gone.
components.title: User-facing orchestrator

components.notes: ⚠️ THE MISSING `tools:` LINE IS THE HAZARD, and it was measured: with no allowlist a child's active set came back as read, bash, edit and write plus every custom tool. Omitting the line does not narrow the child, it hands it a shell. ⚠️ NO ROLE DECLARES A MODEL in this version; a role-shipped model would silently override the operator's project selection. ⚠️ THE CHECK IS THE ROLE-DEFINITION CHECK, not a "roster lint": #18 and #143 settled that this project has no artifact roster, and this component's "specialist roster" is an unrelated object. ⚠️ THIS COMPONENT DECLARES; IT DOES NOT RUN. What a real child actually receives is CMP-0036's, measured by ACC-0076.
components.responsibility: Declare the research, planning and validation roles as data: stable name and description, an explicit tool allowlist, input contract, responsibilities, forbidden actions, output schema, exit criteria and escalation conditions. Derive write boundaries and required tool signatures from the existing specialist contract rather than restating them, and treat a role definition with no declared tool list as a role-definition check failure.
components.title: Specialist roster

components.notes:
⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-19 (TSK-0052 landed). This note used to say the verifier contradicted the spawn contract, because `verifyChild` refused unless `stdinDelivered` was true while the approved contract closes stdin. That is fixed: the field is now `taskBindingObserved`, the refusal key is `CHILD_REFUSED.NO_TASK_BINDING` with the wire value `task-not-delivered` unchanged, and one test asserts both facts at once over each retained platform record - stdin closed, and the exact task reaching the child's model turn.

⚠️ WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS COMPONENT. `verifyChild` CONSUMES the observation and never makes it. Producing it during a real launch is this component's own work, under TSK-0053: a private Kiln observer extension loaded explicitly into the child inspects the final provider payload in `before_provider_request` and attests, over a dedicated extra pipe, that the framed task was there. Model output and ordinary JSON events are not acceptable sources, because both let the child vouch for itself; nor is writing or hashing the prompt file, which proves preparation rather than consumption.

⚠️ THE REFUSAL MATRIX IS BUILT (TSK-0054, 2026-09-20). `verifyChild` still consumes rather than observes, and it is now the LAST of seven ordered checks rather than the only one. The runtime refuses a timeout or abort, an unreadable event stream, a nonzero exit, a missing task binding, a contradicted selection and an out-of-role write before it reaches the gate, and the assistant's text is selected only after the gate accepts. The write boundary is `mayWrite` over the canonical operation a wire name resolves to, so one definition governs both the wrapper and the child.
components.responsibility: Run a specialist as an isolated Pi child and decide whether its answer may be used: build a task-scoped context rather than forwarding the conversation, bind the role prompt and the task through a private file with restrictive permissions and closed stdin, pass the orchestrator's exact provider, model and thinking level, pass the intersection of the role's allowlist and the measured host registry, enforce a bounded timeout, delete temporary material on every exit path, and verify the child's capability signature before reading its substantive output.
components.title: Delegation runtime

components.notes: ⚠️ ONE TERMINAL, TWO PROCESSES, AND ONLY ONE MAY READ IT. If the background launcher inherits stdin it will eat the authentication answer or the first planning message. ⚠️ PI'S WORKING DIRECTORY IS THE OUTER PROJECT, never the tool clone, and the self-hosting checkout — where those two are the same directory — is refused unless explicitly opted into. F122 (2026-09-16): CI run 35097288227, at commit b8b09b2, windows-latest node 22, natural mode. The launch preflight timed out on the primed WMI route at 10,009.7 ms with no rows, and the supervisor refused with process-table-not-primed before either Pi or the launcher was spawned. ACC-0081's 10-second preflight bound held as specified, so the criterion outcome stands. This is the second primed-route timeout event that EVD-0109's recorded rule names: WMI is withdrawn as the Windows identity strategy and replaced wholesale by a WMI-free identity format, delivered as a separate correction. The later green run 35141902017 does not cancel it. Interactive session recovery for ACC-0103 is paused until the replacement is green. F130 (2026-09-17, watch item): CI run 35214314607 at commit a957d43, windows-latest node 22, interrupt evidence. One WMI-free identity read for the launcher tree started 5,384 ms into the shutdown with a 2,316 ms allowance and did not answer (process-table-timeout); the other seven Windows reads in that cell took 362 to 530 ms. With 298 ms left no further read was started, the launcher descendant was recorded unverified, and the run refused with shutdown-not-observed at 7,706 of 8,000 ms. The deadline and fail-closed behaviour held. The failed job was not rerun and production shutdown behaviour is unchanged. If another Windows CI run times out on a WMI-free identity read, phase instrumentation of identity reads (spawn, first byte, exit) follows. F130 recurred in the same run on windows-latest node 24: five consecutive WMI-free reads ran to the full 10,000 ms bound (four real-reader tests and the natural evidence preflight, which refused the launch before spawning), while later reads in that cell took 245 to 638 ms. Under the recorded rule, O6 phase instrumentation is active. F133 (2026-09-17, watch item): CI run 35250274939 at commit 3a2a830, windows-latest node 22. The unit test 'a descendant that survives its parent is escalated, and the tree is not reported stopped' reported no surviving descendant where it expected one. It injects its processes but uses real timers (200 ms grace, 150 ms hard wait, a 30 ms parent exit), and the commit under test changed only the guard-file module. Not investigated. If it recurs, that test's real-time dependency is replaced with deterministic clock controls; its waits are not increased. ⚠️ ITS REFUSAL CLASSES AND EXIT CODES ARE UNCOVERED (2026-09-24, corrected from CMP-0020). ACC-0084 covers `bin/setup.mjs` only: it evaluates CMP-0039, and it was amended to that command because the launch-side classes cannot be observed through setup — its selection phase refuses first in every case that would reach the preflight. So nothing currently measures that the refusal classes raised on the way to a running Kiln — launch failure, a committed selection that cannot be used, and the rest of `LaunchRefusal`'s reasons — each exit with a distinct published code. TSK-0037 carries the obligation. EVD-0139 states the boundary from setup's side.
components.responsibility: Own the lifecycle of the two processes that make up a running Kiln: validate the project and settings, choose and prove a port, start the browser launcher with a private stdin pipe so it cannot consume the operator's typing, wait for identity-confirmed readiness, start Pi in the outer project root with the terminal inherited, begin or resume the recorded planning session, and on exit or signal stop both process trees within bounded grace periods and remove only what this invocation created.
components.title: Combined runtime supervisor

components.notes: ⚠️ ITS PRE-INSTALL IMPORT GRAPH IS BUILT-INS ONLY. Setup runs before the dependency graph it installs exists, so a top-level import of Pi, Ajv or anything else installed is not a style question — the command cannot start. Everything after the install step is loaded dynamically. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A SECOND INITIALIZER: `bin/init-project.mjs` keeps its content-only contract and its refusal semantics. ⚠️ THE INSTALL COMES BEFORE THE TRANSACTION PLAN (D26, 2026-09-22). The dependency install comes before the transaction plan because the plan validates existing Kiln records, and that validation needs Ajv, which the install is what provides. Everything up to and including the install is therefore built-ins only (ACC-0083), and the install is a bootstrap mutation confined to the .planning checkout: it changes no consumer project state and does not rewrite the lockfile. An interruption during the bootstrap has no journal to resume from, and must leave consumer project state unchanged.
components.responsibility: Compose the whole first run in one ordered, resumable, idempotent command over the existing primitives: resolve and print every path before mutating, validate the runtime, take the setup lock, install the locked dependencies as a bootstrap mutation confined to the .planning checkout, then plan the transaction, run the existing initializer under it, establish state protection, install and register the package, obtain each consent in its own step, bind and prove the model, read back everything it wrote, and either launch the combined runtime or explain exactly what remains. Use a distinct exit code per refusal class and publish the mapping.
components.title: Setup command

components.notes: ⚠️ THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS CARRY MORE WEIGHT THAN THE HAPPY PATH, because every one of them corresponds to a way this layer can appear to work while being wrong: wrong working directory, inspection denied, a read attempted before consent, a sole model adopted implicitly, a TTY-less login, a denied live check, Tavily contacted before approval, trust denied, an unrelated healthy HTTP service on the port, signature drift, and a fake child returning plausible prose with none of Kiln's tools.
components.responsibility: Prove the documented journey from an empty directory on both supported platforms: initialise a repository with no commits, take a tracked-file-only copy of the tool as the clone, run the documented setup against a deterministic non-billable provider, drive a Stage 1 exchange, observe the intake document change through the browser's change stream, attempt an unauthorised stage advance and see it refused, shut down and prove nothing is left running, then rerun and prove resumption and idempotency.
components.title: Clean-consumer agent-delivery verification

components.notes: ⚠️ IT IS A GATE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. Every design position downstream of it was an assumption carried from measurements taken on a different version. ⚠️ NEGATIVE EVIDENCE REQUIRES PROOF THAT THE OBSERVATION POINT WAS REACHED, and every run records whether it did. ⚠️ TWO TIERS: the default one asserts over the retained results and FAILS when package.json's pin no longer matches the pin the evidence was taken under; the live tier re-runs the spike against a real consumer install behind KILN_PI_COMPAT=live, on one CI cell. Both are held to the SAME assertion function, because a live tier that checks less than the record is a live tier in name only. ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-09-03 AFTER REVIEW, and the removals matter more than the additions. THREE THINGS THIS COMPONENT NO LONGER CLAIMS: Pi's interactive /login in the full TUI and what the same launch does with no TTY (TSK-0065; Pi 0.84.4 has no authentication-only launch); OAuth discovery, which a models.json provider structurally cannot exercise (QST-0033, TSK-0066), and which a manual account-bound Windows run has since verified for openai-codex (EVD-0124, ACC-0091), outside this suite; and the Kiln capability signature, which could not be measured then because the Kiln package it belongs to did not exist yet (TSK-0067, against CMP-0031). The package now exists, and TSK-0067 has measured the signature: presence in EVD-0106, and refusal of a changed tool signature read from a real session in EVD-0122, recorded by this suite's retained runs and re-proved by the live tier with the same assertion in CI run 35591168378, on ubuntu-latest node 24 only. Each is scheduled rather than quietly dropped. The earlier wording listed all three as established, which is exactly the failure — a component describing work that was not there — that this whole cycle was opened to undo.
components.responsibility: Establish, against the exact pinned runtime and on each supported platform, what Pi actually does where the agent-delivery design depends on it — local resolution from a consumer's own install and version match; trust grant, denial and revocation through the public API; saved API-key discovery and provider auth status; configuration-directory resolution under default and overridden settings; the literal package entry `pi install -l` writes and its canonical equivalence to the committed form; extension, skill and prompt loading; skill-override precedence; session relocation; task binding with closed stdin; the default and allowlisted tool sets; and provider-scoped environment authentication reaching a child — each with a negative control and redaction assertions, retained as tests in the normal suite so a later version bump must re-prove the contract rather than inherit it.
components.title: Pi compatibility evidence suite

note: Generated as a query over the task graph, grouped by `task.role` (#19). Nothing here is authored: re-running the handoff recomputes it, so a slice cannot drift from the plan. `tasks` is work REMAINING; `accepted` is work already finished, listed so nobody repeats it. Both statuses are derived from acceptance criteria, never stored.

requirements.rationale: Intake: 'session quality is inconsistent' — the process is currently negotiated per session.
requirements.statement: The system must define the sequence of planning activities and their completion conditions, such that two planning sessions on comparable projects follow the same sequence.
requirements.title: The planning process is defined by the system, not by the session

requirements.rationale: Intake: the PM cannot currently tell how far a planning session has got.
requirements.statement: At any point the system must be able to report which stage the project is in and what that stage still requires.
requirements.title: Current project state is inspectable at any time

requirements.rationale: Intake problem 2: 'educated guessing' on vendor docs, OS procedures, versions and known issues.
requirements.statement: When a planning question depends on external fact, the system must be able to consult a current external source rather than reason from what it already holds.
requirements.title: Implementation questions can be answered from current external sources

requirements.rationale: Intake problem 3: no sandbox, so testable assumptions are inferred instead.
requirements.statement: The system must be able to execute a procedure in a real environment and capture the commands run, the output produced, and whether it succeeded.
requirements.title: Claims can be tested by execution in a real environment

requirements.rationale: A procedure that worked somewhere unlike the target has not been validated for the target.
requirements.statement: Any claim validated by execution must record the environment it ran in, in enough detail to judge whether that environment resembles the target.
requirements.title: A tested claim records the environment it was tested in

requirements.rationale: Intake: 'the runbook should represent the output of discovery, not the beginning of discovery.'
requirements.statement: No instruction in the final output may rest on a claim whose basis is below the level required for that instruction.
requirements.title: Instructions rest on resolved claims

requirements.rationale: Intake objective, stated in the PM's own terms.
requirements.statement: A recipient of the output must be able to begin their part of the work without asking the planner for information the plan should have contained.
requirements.title: The handoff is actionable without returning to the planner

requirements.rationale: Intake stakeholders: the material explicitly declines to assume which the implementer is. This is testable by comparing both consumers against the same required-information inventory.
requirements.statement: For every required item in the handoff, both a human reader and an automated consumer must be able to recover the same information without depending on the other representation.
requirements.title: The output serves a human or an agent implementer

requirements.rationale: Intake constraint: validation cannot assume a free, local, consequence-free environment.
requirements.statement: The system must not perform a validation that incurs cost or uses credentials unless the operator has explicitly authorised that class of validation.
requirements.title: Validation that costs money or needs credentials requires explicit authorisation

requirements.rationale: Intake: 'continuously capture decisions and evolving requirements.' A decision without alternatives cannot be reopened intelligently.
requirements.statement: Every decision that shapes the plan must be recorded together with the options considered and why the chosen one won.
requirements.title: Decisions are recorded with their alternatives

requirements.rationale: Intake open questions 1-4 are themselves examples: they need to survive being read once.
requirements.statement: An unresolved question must exist as a tracked item with a state, not as a sentence inside a document.
requirements.title: Open questions are tracked objects, not prose

requirements.rationale: REQ-0002 requires current project state to be inspectable at any time, and stage position is the coarsest form of that state. Deriving it rather than storing it follows #16: stage status is derived from artifacts, never persisted alongside them.
requirements.statement: The application shows which stage the project is in, derived from the stage definitions and the recorded attestations rather than from a stored status value.
requirements.title: The application displays the project's current stage

requirements.rationale: Stage documents are the narrative half of the plan and are agent-authored. Rendering them is the point of choosing MDX; bounding what they may execute is what keeps content from becoming application code.
requirements.statement: The application renders the MDX stage document for a selected stage, and a document referencing a component outside the permitted set does not execute arbitrary code.
requirements.title: The application renders a stage document authored in MDX

requirements.rationale: The agent and the operator write the same files (#15), so a view that only refreshes on reload shows state that has already moved. The second clause is the harder half: a silently dead stream renders stale content that looks live.
requirements.statement: When a file under the content root is changed by something other than the application, the application's view updates without the operator reloading the page, and a dropped update stream is visibly distinguishable from an idle one.
requirements.title: The application reflects external content changes without a manual reload

requirements.rationale: #88 forbids authoring content by any route but a typed operation, and #78 plus #72 make the write safe against the agent writing concurrently. A second write path in the app would be a second protocol against the same files.
requirements.statement: A review-status change made in the application is written by the existing typed operation — lock, fresh read inside the lock, atomic write — and the application contains no other write path into content.
requirements.title: The application performs review-status updates through the existing typed write path

requirements.rationale: The product is a local-first tool a consumer clones (#1, #20, #32). An application whose supported mode is undeclared cannot be validated against the configuration it actually ships in — which is why AST-0010 is deferred rather than answered.
requirements.statement: An operator can install and start the application on a clean machine from documented commands, and the supported deployment mode is stated rather than implied.
requirements.title: The application is installable and runnable locally from a documented command

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THIS IS AN ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENT, NOT A TESTING PREFERENCE, and the distinction is what AST-0022 establishes. 'Verify it behaves correctly' is unavailable here as a matter of measured fact rather than of rigour — the observable behaviour of a compliant and a non-compliant read is IDENTICAL on a route that has at least one compliant read. The property has to be enforced where it is visible, which is in the source. ⚠️ TWO OBLIGATIONS, and the second is the one that gets forgotten: confine the read, AND check the boundary. DEC-0019 requires both `connection()` before the read and a `<Suspense>` boundary around it, and an abstraction can supply the first while a caller omits the second. A check that only looks for stray `readFileSync` calls would pass an application whose every read is correctly routed and unboundaried — which builds fine without Cache Components and FAILS THE BUILD with it, so the omission surfaces as a configuration change breaking the build rather than as the contract violation it is. ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS DELIBERATELY UNSPECIFIED. A lint rule, a module-boundary constraint, a generated single accessor, or a build step that greps for content-root paths would each satisfy this; choosing among them is stage 5 design work that belongs with the components, and naming one here would decide it before the components exist. What is fixed is the PROPERTY: checkable without executing the application. ⚠️ IT INTERACTS WITH QST-0018 AND DOES NOT PRE-EMPT IT. If a stage document may reference components, then the permitted-component set is also a surface through which a direct read could enter, and static confinement has to cover it. That is a constraint QST-0018's answer must satisfy, not a decision about what that answer is. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT SETTLE CACHE COMPONENTS. DEC-0019 was chosen precisely so the contract holds with that flag either way, and a static check on source has nothing to say about it. Any enforcement design that only works under one setting would spend the property DEC-0019 bought. ⚠️ SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-27 BY DEC-0021: the same static check must also enforce that no application module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, and must detect bypass paths. It is one more forbidden edge in the same import graph, not a second mechanism — and it is the same failure shape as AST-0022, because the adapter boundary is a convention that nothing observable distinguishes from a violation: an app module importing `lib/` directly behaves identically until someone renders it from a client component.
requirements.rationale: AST-0022 measured that a read violating the contract is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route — the compliant read makes the route dynamic and the violation rides along. So a behavioural check cannot see the violation: every freshness test passes on a codebase that breaks the contract, right up until the compliant sibling is moved, cached or deleted, at which point every read on that route silently reverts to build-time content. A test that passes on broken code is worse than no test, because it is also a claim that the code was checked.
requirements.statement: Every read of planning content in the application goes through a single reading abstraction that applies the DEC-0019 contract. A direct filesystem read of the content root anywhere else in the application fails a check that does not depend on running the application or observing what it serves, and the same check verifies that each read site is enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary. Acceptance for REQ-0016, REQ-0017 and REQ-0018 may not rest on freshness behaviour alone.
requirements.title: Planning-content reads are confined to the approved abstraction, and the confinement is checked statically

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THE REFUSAL HALF IS NOT DECORATION. Setup touches an operator's credentials, trust store, ports and money; the number of ways it can legitimately stop is larger than the number of ways it can succeed. A command that succeeds or hangs is worse than one that refuses precisely, which is why the phase and the resume command are in the statement rather than in the error-handling section of a design document.
requirements.rationale: The product is a planning conversation that writes structured content and shows it in a browser. Until 2026-09-02 the documented consumer path ended at `npm --prefix .planning start`, which starts the browser and nothing else: Pi started nowhere, so the half of the product that does the planning was unreachable by any documented route. A requirement that says `installable and runnable` (REQ-0020) was satisfied by that state, which is how the gap stayed invisible.
requirements.statement: From a machine that has Git and the supported Node version and nothing else of Kiln's, one documented command must initialise the planning workspace, install the pinned agent runtime, obtain every decision it needs from the operator, and end with the planning agent conversing about this project — or refuse, naming the phase that stopped and an exact command that resumes it. Starting the browser application alone does not satisfy this requirement.
requirements.title: One documented command carries a clean project to a running planning conversation

requirements.notes: ⚠️ 'RECORDED WHERE ANOTHER OPERATOR DOES NOT INHERIT IT' IS THE HALF THAT IS EASY TO LOSE. The project selection is committed configuration and should be; the approval to use THIS host's credentials is not. If the two are stored together, cloning the repository hands a second operator the first operator's consent, and nobody ever sees the prompt.
requirements.rationale: Technical access is not consent. Kiln runs on the operator's own machine and can read their Pi configuration trivially, which is exactly why the boundary has to be a decision rather than a capability check. The three permissions are genuinely different questions — a local inspection that contacts nothing, an ongoing authorisation to spend on a named model, and an external call to a third-party service — and collapsing them into one prompt would mean the operator granting the expensive one by answering the cheap one.
requirements.statement: The system must not read the operator's provider authentication store, custom-model registry, or the presence of credential environment variables before the operator has permitted that inspection. Having detected a usable configuration must never by itself authorise adopting or using it. Permission to inspect, confirmation of an exact provider and model, and permission to validate and use an optional external service are three decisions, each granted separately and each recorded where a different operator on a different machine does not inherit it.
requirements.title: Existing configuration is inspected, and then used, only under separately granted permission

requirements.notes: ⚠️ PROCESS ARGUMENTS ARE IN THE LIST DELIBERATELY. Command lines are visible in process listings to other users on the same machine, so passing a key through Pi's `--api-key` option is a disclosure even though nothing is written to disk. ⚠️ SO ARE DERIVED VALUES: a hash or prefix of a key recorded as a cache identity is credential-derived, and a compatibility record keyed on one is a credential artifact wearing a different name.
requirements.rationale: The specialist child environment is the concrete hazard. The existing contract passes base OS variables plus TAVILY_API_KEY for the research role, which is correct for the tool plane and insufficient for the model plane: a provider authenticated only through OPENAI_API_KEY leaves every child unable to infer. The tempting fix — inherit more of the environment — is the one that must be foreclosed by a requirement, because it works immediately and leaks everything.
requirements.statement: No committed project file, emitted log line, error message, generated artifact, test fixture, or constructed process argument may contain a credential value or a value derived from one. A credential reaches a subprocess only through an audited contract that names, for one selected provider, the exact environment-variable names required; a provider with no such recorded mapping is refused rather than granted a wider inheritance of the operator's environment.
requirements.title: Credential material never enters project files, logs, process arguments, or planning content

requirements.notes: ⚠️ 'EXPLICITLY SELECTED' BINDS EVEN WHEN DISCOVERY RETURNS EXACTLY ONE MODEL. A single available model is a discovery result, not a decision, and adopting it silently is the same class of act as adopting the global default. ⚠️ THE PROOF COSTS MONEY, which is why it is a separate authorisation and not a step: see the consent requirement.
requirements.rationale: Two silent failures are being closed at once. A registry entry proves configuration and not that the endpoint answers or that the model will emit a correctly shaped tool call, so a zero-cost preflight cannot be the last word. And a fallback to a global default would mean the project's recorded content was produced by a model the project never named, which destroys the only reproducibility claim the configuration makes.
requirements.statement: The provider and exact model used for planning work must be chosen by the operator from what discovery reports, recorded as reproducible non-secret project configuration naming exact identifiers rather than a mutable alias, and proven able to perform the tool calls the system depends on before the system describes the agent as ready. When the recorded selection cannot be resolved or authenticated, the system must refuse to begin or resume planning work rather than substituting another model, another provider, or its own memory.
requirements.title: Agent work runs on an explicitly selected and proven model, or it does not run

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THIS IS THE OPEN HALF OF DECISION #67. Half of that decision — recording a trust grant so children come up trusted — has been executed and measured. The detection half has never been built, and it is the half that holds when the grant is missing, revoked, or made on a different machine.
requirements.rationale: Measured on 2026-08-15 and not since mitigated: a non-interactive Pi child launched against an untrusted project loads no package, therefore none of Kiln's typed tools, and DOES NOT ERROR. The session completes, turn_start and turn_end and agent_end all fire, and the model answers in freehand prose. Every role boundary in this system is enforced by typed tools, so a child without them is not a degraded specialist — it is an unconstrained model whose output looks exactly like a specialist's.
requirements.statement: Before any part of a specialist's substantive answer is read or acted on, the system must observe that the child ran with the capability signature and tool set its role contract requires. A child that exited cleanly, emitted a well-formed transcript, and did not have those tools must fail the delegation loudly; its prose must not be accepted as the answer to the delegated task.
requirements.title: A delegated result is used only when the child that produced it is proven to have had its tools

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THE ORDERING IS THE OPERATIONAL HALF. A design that puts transcripts under an ignored path is correct and still leaks if the first transcript is written before the ignore rule exists, or if the operator deleted the rule and setup carried on. The safe sequence and the refusal that follows a missing rule are both part of the requirement.
requirements.rationale: The tool clone at `.planning/` is updated with `git pull`, so anything runtime written inside it is state the update channel is entitled to destroy. The outer project is version-controlled by the operator, so anything runtime written there is state Git is entitled to publish. Both halves of that sentence have to hold at once, which is why the requirement names an ordering — coverage first, then data — rather than only a location.
requirements.statement: Session transcripts, launch state, consent records, compatibility results and setup journals must be written where updating the tool clone cannot destroy them and where ordinary version control does not track them, while reproducible non-secret project configuration remains committed and reviewable. The system must not write runtime state into a location before the ignore coverage protecting that location is in place.
requirements.title: Runtime state survives a tool update and never enters version control

requirements.notes: ⚠️ THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS TESTABLE, and it should be written before the check: stand up an unrelated healthy HTTP server on the port and require launch to refuse. A readiness check without that control has never been shown to check anything.
requirements.rationale: The current launcher polls `GET /` on the configured port and treats any HTTP response as ready. An unrelated service already listening on port 3000 therefore satisfies it, and the operator is told the browser workspace is up while looking at somebody else's application. The same shape recurs across the layer: an extension that loaded, a model that replied, a session that resumed — each is only evidence if something distinguishes it from a lookalike.
requirements.statement: Before reporting a component ready, the system must confirm the identity of whatever responded: that the HTTP service answering the port is the process this invocation started and is serving this project, that the loaded package is the one it installed, and that the model answering is the one recorded. A response that merely arrives, from an unidentified source, is not readiness and must not be reported as such.
requirements.title: A readiness claim names what answered

tasks.notes: ⚠️ CONSENT REUSE REQUIRES A CONCLUSIVE GIT CHECK. An unchanged project is not asked again only where Git gives a definite answer that the consent record is in neither the index nor HEAD and is ignored by the repository that holds it, or that no repository holds it. Without such an answer no saved answer is trusted or written, the answer applies only to the current run, and the operator is told so (NOT_REMEMBERED.unverified in lib/consent-record.mjs). The clean-machine requirement already specifies Git. Component proof in EVD-0126.
tasks.statement: Persist the host-specific grant in the ignored local-state root, keyed so that a provider or research change invalidates it, and read it at launch so an unchanged project does not re-prompt while a new machine does.
tasks.title: Build the local consent record and its invalidation rules

tasks.statement: After a separate approval, run the existing `GET /usage` capability probe from `lib/research/tavily-adapter.mjs`, persist the non-secret project choice and the local approval, and map each internal state to its required user-facing wording. Declining leaves research unavailable and does not block planning.
tasks.title: Implement the Tavily consent, probe and plain-English outcomes

tasks.notes: ⚠️ LOGIN SELECTS A MODEL; KILN STILL REQUIRES ITS OWN CHOICE (F14, EVD-0123). After an API-key /login, Pi printed 'Selected gpt-5.5' and the session switched to that model. Whether Pi persisted it was not established. Kiln must still require its own explicit model choice after login and must not treat the model Pi selected as the operator's selection.
tasks.statement: Present available providers and exact model identifiers, validate any supplied `--provider`/`--model`/`--thinking` against the registry, require confirmation, state the billing consequence, and persist the exact identifiers through the settings merge per DEC-0028.
tasks.title: Build model discovery, explicit selection and persistence

tasks.statement: Register `kiln_preflight` outside the orchestrator registry, accepting only the one-time challenge schema and returning a fixed acknowledgement with no access to content, mutation, research, validation, delegation or shell; issue the canary under a low token ceiling and remove the tool from the effective set before the user-facing session starts.
tasks.title: Build the setup-only preflight tool and the bounded canary request

tasks.notes: ⚠️ LAUNCH CONSUMES THIS KEY (TSK-0037, B1). The expected compatibility key must be computable at every launch from the current runtime inputs, independently of the stored record, and passed to checkLaunch as expectedKey. A different-model one-run override must have a route to obtain matching compatibility proof for that model, so the override TSK-0037 offers as a remedy can start a run.
tasks.statement: Check configuration, auth availability, model resolution, package loading and tool signatures at no cost; store canary success keyed to its exact inputs in the local-state root; and implement every invalidation input so a changed key reopens approval.
tasks.title: Build the zero-cost preflight and the compatibility record

The fixture TSK-0062 built is a custom provider, and TSK-0072 made such a project startable (accepted 2026-09-24, ACC-0116 on EVD-0142). What that start does not cover stays here: the Stage 1 exchange and the interactive-terminal observation, because its Pi read piped input rather than a terminal. ⚠️ 2026-09-24 (EVD-0145): the automated journey is built and passes in all four cells of CI run 36065687783, which was red overall because of F130. ACC-0086 and ACC-0087 pass. ACC-0088 stays not-evaluated for its manual Windows Node 24 immediate-quit run, and ACC-0114 for its real-model review. The journey found and fixed F12 through F16. F17, an Ubuntu Node 22 cancellation at 45 minutes, is unexplained. The README's sequence is now setup and the launcher. F1, THE JOURNEY TEST'S HEADLESS CHROME, OPEN WITH A RECORDED LIMIT (2026-09-26). The test's own browser sometimes never becomes ready on Windows: seen in CI runs 36178450744 (Node 22) and 36197842986 (Node 24), and in focused Windows journey runs 1 of 4 (36180776736, none), 1 of 8 (36199281598) and 1 of 8 (36204554670), each after Kiln's first run had passed its shutdown checks. What the bounded diagnostics establish (a873d83, d9b31ae, 2f6d6fa; capture retained outside the repository, D:\work\kiln-job-manual\f1-browser-capture-2026-09-26\browser-diag.jsonl, sha256 8a5f0231d0b2e5cb146d21f084396bf3fce1638a661decc6b6f66117c70500ec): the launched chrome.exe (pid 7028, a child of the test's own node process) was created at 00:26:34.410Z and never exited; its only child (pid 6620) appeared 2.8 s later; no other Chrome process ever started; Chrome wrote nothing to stderr in 30 s although the same verbose-logging flags produce about 41 KB in 3 s on a healthy start; DevToolsActivePort never appeared. The process-table read that returned no rows in run 36199281598 succeeded in 36204554670 (140 rows, 1.1 s); why it failed earlier was not recorded. Include one run that cannot be automated and must be performed at a real terminal: on Windows and Node 24, quit the interactive session IMMEDIATELY after a completed tool call, and record what the process and the supervisor did.
